paths.title: Meet Jesus
paths.subtitle: His life, his words and who he is, one short story at a time.

lessons.title: A promise to Mary
lessons.prayer: God, when your plans surprise me, help me trust you the way Mary did: let it be done as you say.

cards.text: God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth in Galilee, to Mary, a virgin pledged to be married to a man named Joseph. Gabriel said, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.” She would have a son and name him Jesus.

Her son would be called the Son of the Most High, and his Kingdom would have no end. Mary asked how, since she was a virgin. Gabriel said the Holy Spirit would come on her, and that her relative Elizabeth was expecting a son in her old age.
The angel ended with this: “nothing spoken by God is impossible.” Mary had asked an honest question, and the answer she got was a promise. You can bring God your honest questions too.
Mary said, “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.

cards.question: To which town did God send the angel Gabriel?
cards.explain: Luke says Gabriel was sent from God “to a city of Galilee named Nazareth.”

cards.question: Which relative of Mary was also expecting a son?
cards.explain: Gabriel told Mary, “Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age.”

cards.text: Mary had a real question, and she still said yes to God: let it be done according to your word.

lessons.title: Born in Bethlehem
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you came to ordinary people on an ordinary night. Help me make room for you today.

cards.text: Caesar Augustus ordered a census, so Joseph, who was of David’s family, went from Nazareth to Bethlehem, David’s city, with Mary, who was pregnant. There she gave birth to her firstborn son and laid him in a manger, because there was no room in the inn.

Nearby, shepherds were keeping watch over their flock by night. An angel appeared and said, “Don’t be afraid.” A Savior was born in David’s city, and they would find him lying in a feeding trough. Then a multitude of angels praised God.
The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem, found the baby just as they had been told, and went home praising God. Mary kept it all in her heart. God’s good news is worth going to see for yourself.

The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people. For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.”

cards.question: Why was the baby laid in a manger?
choices: There was no room in the inn
cards.answer: There was no room in the inn
cards.explain: Luke says Mary laid him in a feeding trough “because there was no room for them in the inn.”

cards.question: Who did the angel visit with the news that night?
cards.explain: Luke says an angel stood by shepherds who were “keeping watch by night over their flock” and told them a Savior was born.

cards.text: The Savior was born and laid in a feeding trough, and an angel brought the news to shepherds in the fields.

lessons.title: Visitors from the east
lessons.prayer: Jesus, the wise men traveled far just to worship you. Lead me to you today, and fill me with their joy.

cards.text: In the days of King Herod, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem asking, “Where is he who is born King of the Jews?” Herod was troubled. When the chief priests and scribes said the Christ would be born in Bethlehem, he sent the wise men there and asked them to report back.

The star went ahead of them and stopped over the place where the child was, and they rejoiced with great joy. They bowed down and worshiped him, gave gold, frankincense and myrrh, then went home another way after a warning in a dream.

Then an angel warned Joseph in a dream to flee to Egypt, because Herod would seek the child to destroy him. Joseph left by night. The warning came before the danger did. God can guide you one step at a time too.

When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy. They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

cards.question: What led the wise men to the place where the child was?
cards.explain: Matthew says the star “went before them until it came and stood over where the young child was.”

cards.question: Where did the angel tell Joseph to take the child and his mother?
cards.explain: The angel said to Joseph in a dream, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt.”

cards.text: Visitors from the east followed a star to worship Jesus, and God kept the child safe from Herod.

lessons.title: The boy in the temple
lessons.prayer: Father, like the boy Jesus, I want to feel at home with you. Help me grow in wisdom today.

cards.text: Every year Jesus’ parents went to Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover. When he was 12, Jesus stayed behind without them knowing. They traveled a whole day, searched among their relatives, then went back to Jerusalem to look for him.

After 3 days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions. All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers. His mother told him they had been anxiously looking for him.
Jesus answered, “Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?” Then he went home, obeyed his parents and kept growing in wisdom and stature. You can belong to God and still be growing too.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

cards.question: How old was Jesus when he stayed behind in Jerusalem?
cards.explain: Luke says “When he was twelve years old,” they went up to Jerusalem for the feast, and as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind.

cards.question: Where did his parents find Jesus after 3 days?
cards.explain: Luke says “they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers,” listening and asking questions.

cards.text: At 12, Jesus was at home in his Father’s house, and he kept growing in wisdom and favor.

lessons.title: A voice in the wilderness
lessons.prayer: Jesus, John pointed past himself to you. Let my life point to you today.

cards.text: Mark opens with “The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” Then he quotes the prophets: God would send a messenger ahead, a voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord.

Then John came, baptizing in the wilderness and preaching “the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.” People from Judea and Jerusalem came, confessing their sins. He wore camel’s hair and ate locusts and wild honey.
Crowds came to John, yet he kept pointing to someone else: one so mighty that John said he wasn’t worthy to untie his sandals. You don’t have to be the center of the story. Jesus is.

As it is written in the prophets, “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you: the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’”

cards.question: What did John eat?
cards.explain: Mark says John wore camel’s hair and a leather belt, and he “ate locusts and wild honey.”

cards.question: John said the one coming after him would baptize people in what?
cards.explain: John said, “I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”

cards.text: John prepared the way and pointed to Jesus, the mightier one, who would baptize in the Holy Spirit.

lessons.title: The baptism
lessons.prayer: Father, thank you that I am loved before I do anything. Help me hear that today.

cards.text: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John. John tried to stop him: “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?” Jesus said it was the fitting way to fulfill all righteousness, so John agreed.
As soon as Jesus was baptized and went up from the water, the heavens were opened to him. He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming on him.
Then a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.” In Matthew, Jesus had not yet preached or done a single miracle. Love came first, and it comes first for you too.
Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”

cards.question: What came down on Jesus as a dove?
cards.explain: Matthew says Jesus saw “the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming on him.”

cards.question: John the Baptist first tried to stop Jesus from being baptized.
cards.explain: John said, “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?” Then Jesus answered, and John allowed it.

cards.text: Before Jesus did a single miracle, the Father said: this is my beloved Son.

lessons.title: Tested in the wilderness
lessons.prayer: Jesus, when I am tempted, help me hold on to what God has said, the way you did.

cards.text: After his baptism, the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. He fasted 40 days and 40 nights and was hungry. The tempter said: if you are the Son of God, turn these stones into bread. Jesus answered with Scripture.

Next the devil set him on the pinnacle of the temple and told him to throw himself down, quoting Scripture himself. Then he offered all the kingdoms of the world for one act of worship. Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan!” The devil left, and angels served him.
Three times Jesus answered, “It is written,” using words from Deuteronomy. When you feel pulled, you don’t have to win the argument. You can stand on what God has already said.
But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God’s mouth.’”

cards.question: What did the devil first tell Jesus to turn into bread?
cards.explain: The tempter said, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”

cards.question: The devil quoted Scripture when he tempted Jesus.
cards.explain: On the pinnacle of the temple, the devil said “it is written” and quoted words about angels bearing Jesus up.

cards.text: In the wilderness, Jesus met every temptation with God’s word, and the devil left him.

lessons.title: Come, follow me
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you call ordinary people in the middle of ordinary days. Help me follow you today.

cards.text: Passing along the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting a net, because they were fishermen. He called them to come after him and promised to make them fishers for men. Immediately they left their nets and followed him.

A little farther on, he saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee, in their boat mending nets. He called them too, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and went after him.

Jesus called them in the middle of an ordinary workday. He didn’t ask them to become something first. He said, “I will make you into fishers for men.” The making is his work, and that is good news for you.
Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”

cards.question: What were Simon and Andrew doing when Jesus called them?
choices: Casting a net into the sea
cards.answer: Casting a net into the sea
cards.explain: Mark says Jesus saw them “casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.”

cards.question: Who did James and John leave behind in the boat?
cards.explain: Mark says they left “their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.”

cards.text: Jesus called 2 pairs of brothers in the middle of their workday, and they left and followed him.

lessons.title: Water into wine
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you care about ordinary days. I bring you what is running out in my life, and I trust you with it.

cards.text: At a wedding in Cana of Galilee, the wine ran out. Jesus’ mother told him, “They have no wine.” He said his hour had not yet come. His mother told the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”

There were 6 stone water pots. Jesus had the servants fill them to the brim with water, then take some to the ruler of the feast. When he tasted it, it had become wine. He told the bridegroom, “You have kept the good wine until now!”

Jesus’ first sign happened at a wedding. The ruler of the feast didn’t know where the wine came from, but the servants who did what Jesus said knew. Nothing in your everyday life is too small to bring to him.
This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

cards.question: How many stone water pots were there?
cards.explain: John says there were “six water pots of stone,” and the servants filled them up to the brim.

cards.question: What did Jesus’ mother tell the servants?
choices: Whatever he says to you, do it
Ask the bridegroom what to do
cards.answer: Whatever he says to you, do it
cards.explain: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”

cards.text: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turned water into wine, the first of his signs, and his disciples believed in him.

lessons.title: Nicodemus at night
lessons.prayer: God, thank you for loving the world, and me in it. I bring you my questions, and I trust your Son.

cards.text: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews. He came to Jesus by night and said, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God.”

Jesus told him no one can see God’s Kingdom unless they are born anew. Nicodemus asked how a man could be born when he is old. Jesus said everyone born of the Spirit is like the wind: you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from.
The heart of it is love: “God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.” You can come to him like Nicodemus did, questions and all.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

cards.question: When did Nicodemus come to Jesus?
cards.explain: John says “He came to Jesus by night” and called him a teacher who has come from God.

cards.question: What did Jesus say a person must be to see God’s Kingdom?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.”

cards.text: Nicodemus came at night with questions, and John 3 answers with love: God sent his Son to save the world, not to judge it.

lessons.title: The woman at the well
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you know my whole story and still meet me where I am. Thank you for your living water.

cards.text: Tired from his journey, Jesus sat by Jacob’s well in Samaria. A Samaritan woman came to draw water, and he asked her for a drink. She was surprised, because Jews had no dealings with Samaritans.
Jesus said that if she knew who was asking, she would have asked him for living water. Whoever drinks the water he gives “will never thirst again.” She said, “Sir, give me this water.”
Jesus knew her whole story, even her 5 husbands, and he didn’t end the conversation there. He knows your story too, and he still wants to talk with you.
She said the Messiah was coming. Jesus said, “I am he, the one who speaks to you.” She left her water pot, went into the city and said, “Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done.”
But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.

cards.question: What did Jesus offer the woman at the well?
cards.explain: Jesus told her that if she had asked, “he would have given you living water.”

cards.question: The woman left her water pot and went into the city to tell people about Jesus.
cards.explain: John says she “left her water pot, went away into the city,” and said, “Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done.”

cards.text: Jesus knew all she had done. Her word brought many to believe, and once they heard him, they called him “the Savior of the world.”

lessons.title: Through the roof
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for the people who carry me to you. Help me carry someone to you in prayer today.

cards.text: Jesus was at home in Capernaum, and the crowd was so big there was no room, not even around the door. Four people came carrying a paralyzed man. They couldn’t get near, so they opened up the roof and let down his mat.

Seeing their faith, Jesus told the man his sins were forgiven. Some scribes thought only God can forgive sins. So Jesus showed his authority: he told the man to get up, take his mat and go home. He did, in front of them all, and they glorified God.
The man couldn’t get to Jesus on his own, so 4 people carried him and broke through a roof. Jesus saw “their faith.” You can carry someone to Jesus too, in prayer.
Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”

cards.question: How did the 4 people get the man to Jesus?
choices: They opened the roof and let him down
They waited until the crowd left
They carried him in a back door
cards.answer: They opened the roof and let him down
cards.explain: Mark says “they removed the roof where he was” and let down the mat the man was lying on.

cards.question: What did Jesus say to the man first?
cards.explain: Jesus first said, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.” Then, knowing the scribes’ thoughts, he told the man to get up and go home.

cards.text: Four people carried a man through a roof, and Jesus forgave his sins and sent him home walking.

lessons.title: Dinner with tax collectors
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for sitting with people like me. Help me make room at my table for others.

cards.text: Tax collectors were widely disliked in Jesus’ day. Still, Jesus saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office and said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew got up and followed him.

In the house, many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples. The Pharisees asked his disciples why their teacher ate with them. Jesus heard and said, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.”
Jesus sat at the table with people others looked down on. Like a doctor, he went where the need was. If you feel far from God, you are exactly who he came to call.
But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

cards.question: Where was Matthew when Jesus called him?
cards.explain: Matthew was “sitting at the tax collection office” when Jesus said to him, “Follow me.”

cards.question: Who did Jesus say needs a doctor?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.”

cards.text: Jesus called a tax collector, ate with sinners and said he came to call sinners, not the righteous.

lessons.title: The Beatitudes
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you that your blessing reaches the poor in spirit and the grieving. Shape my heart like yours.

cards.text: Seeing the crowds, Jesus went up onto the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to him, and he began to teach them. This teaching is often called the Sermon on the Mount.

He began with blessings: the poor in spirit, those who mourn, the gentle, those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers and those persecuted for righteousness. Each one comes with a promise.

These are not the people the world usually calls lucky. Jesus starts with the poor in spirit, the grieving and the gentle, and calls them blessed. If you feel low today, you are not left out of God’s blessing.
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.

cards.question: Who did Jesus say shall be called children of God?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.”

cards.question: What did Jesus promise to those who mourn?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.”

cards.text: Jesus calls blessed the poor in spirit, the grieving and the gentle, and every blessing comes with a promise.

lessons.title: Salt, light and enemies
lessons.prayer: Father, let my light point to you, and help me pray for someone who is hard to love.

cards.text: Jesus told his listeners, “You are the salt of the earth” and “You are the light of the world.” No one hides a lamp under a basket. Let your light shine, he said, so people may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
People had heard it said: love your neighbor and hate your enemy. But Jesus said, “love your enemies, bless those who curse you,” and pray for those who mistreat you.
God sends sun and rain on the evil and the good. Even tax collectors love those who love them back. When you pray for someone who hurt you, you look like your Father.
Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

cards.question: Where does Jesus say people put a lit lamp?
cards.explain: Jesus said a lamp doesn’t go under a measuring basket, “but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.”

cards.question: On whom does the Father make his sun rise?
cards.explain: Jesus said the Father “makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.”

cards.text: You are salt and light, and you show you are the Father’s child by loving even your enemies.

lessons.title: Teach us to pray
lessons.prayer: Father, thank you that you know what I need before I ask. Teach me to pray to you simply and honestly.

cards.text: Jesus said not to pray to be seen, like people who pray on street corners so others will notice. Go into your room, shut the door and pray to your Father in secret. And you don’t need to pile up words: “your Father knows what things you need before you ask him”.

Then Jesus gave a pattern for prayer, now known as the Lord’s Prayer. It starts with God: his name, his Kingdom, his will. Then it asks for daily bread, for forgiveness, and to be delivered from the evil one.
Jesus teaches you to begin with “Our Father in heaven”. You aren’t talking to a stranger or trying to be heard for your many words. You are talking to a Father who already knows what you need.
Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.’”

cards.question: In the prayer Jesus taught, what do we ask God to give us today?
cards.explain: Jesus taught, “Give us today our daily bread.” It is a prayer for what you need, one day at a time.

cards.question: Right after the prayer, Jesus spoke about forgiving other people.
cards.explain: Jesus went on, “if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”

cards.text: Pray to your Father simply and honestly: honor his name, ask for today’s bread, forgive, and ask him to deliver you from the evil one.

lessons.title: Do not worry
lessons.prayer: Father, you feed the birds and clothe the flowers. Help me trust you with tomorrow and seek you first today.

cards.text: Jesus said not to be anxious about what you will eat, drink or wear. Look at the birds: they don’t sow, reap or store food in barns. “Your heavenly Father feeds them.”

Then he pointed to the lilies of the field. They don’t toil or spin, yet even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one of them. If God clothes the grass like that, “won’t he much more clothe you”?
Jesus points from the birds to you: “Aren’t you of much more value than they?” If your Father cares for birds and wildflowers, he cares for you, and he knows everything you need.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

cards.question: What did Jesus say to seek first?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.”

cards.question: Jesus said that being anxious can add time to your life.
cards.explain: Jesus asked, “Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?” Worry can’t add a moment, but your Father’s care is real.

cards.text: You matter more to God than the birds he feeds. Seek him first today, and trust your Father with tomorrow.

lessons.title: The storm obeys
lessons.prayer: Jesus, when the waves rise in my life, remind me that you are in the boat with me. Speak your peace to my heart.

cards.text: One evening Jesus told his disciples, “Let’s go over to the other side.” They set off across the sea in a boat. Then a big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat until it was filling with water.

Jesus was asleep on a cushion in the stern. They woke him: “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?” He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind stopped, and there was a great calm.
Afterward the disciples asked each other, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” The story invites you to ask that question too, and to trust him in your own storm.
He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.

cards.question: What was Jesus doing during the storm, before the disciples woke him?
choices: Sleeping on a cushion in the stern
cards.answer: Sleeping on a cushion in the stern
cards.explain: Mark says “He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion” until the disciples woke him.

cards.question: When the wind stopped, the disciples were greatly afraid.
cards.explain: Mark says “They were greatly afraid” and asked who Jesus could be, since even the wind and the sea obey him.

cards.text: The wind and the sea obeyed Jesus. The one in your boat is stronger than your storm.

lessons.title: Five loaves, two fish
lessons.prayer: Jesus, here is the little I have. Take it, bless it and use it to help others.

cards.text: A great crowd followed Jesus across the Sea of Galilee, because they had seen his signs on the sick. Jesus asked Philip, “Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?” Philip said 200 denarii worth of bread wouldn’t give everyone even a little.

Andrew pointed out a boy with five barley loaves and two fish. Jesus had the people sit down, about 5,000 men. He gave thanks and the food was handed out, as much as they wanted. The leftovers filled 12 baskets.
Andrew asked, “what are these among so many?” In Jesus’ hands, a boy’s five loaves and two fish fed a crowd. What you bring him may feel small, but he can do more with it than you imagine.
Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down, likewise also of the fish as much as they desired.

cards.question: How many baskets of leftovers were gathered?
cards.explain: Jesus said to gather the pieces “that nothing be lost”, and they “filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves”.

cards.question: Which disciple pointed out the boy with the loaves and fish?
cards.explain: Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said, “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish”.

cards.text: A boy’s five loaves and two fish fed about 5,000 men, with 12 baskets left over. Bring Jesus what you have.

lessons.title: Walking on water
lessons.prayer: Jesus, when I start to sink, help me call out to you. Thank you for reaching out your hand to me.

cards.text: Jesus sent the disciples ahead by boat and went up a mountain alone to pray. Out at sea, the wind was against them. In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came walking on the sea. They cried out, “It’s a ghost!” He said, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”

Peter said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.” Jesus said, “Come!” Peter stepped out and walked on the water toward Jesus. But when he saw the strong wind, he was afraid and began to sink.
As Peter began to sink, his prayer was three words: “Lord, save me!” And “Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand”. You can pray that same short prayer whenever you feel yourself going under.
But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”

cards.question: What made Peter afraid as he walked on the water?
choices: He saw that the wind was strong
He saw how far away the shore was
cards.answer: He saw that the wind was strong
cards.explain: Matthew says “when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink”, he cried out to Jesus.

cards.question: What did the disciples in the boat say as they worshiped Jesus?
choices: You are truly the Son of God!
cards.answer: You are truly the Son of God!
cards.explain: When the wind stopped, those in the boat worshiped him, saying, “You are truly the Son of God!”

cards.text: Jesus came to his friends through the storm. When Peter began to sink, Jesus reached out his hand at once.

lessons.title: Who do you say I am?
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Help me know you more each day.

cards.text: Near Caesarea Philippi, north of the Sea of Galilee, Jesus asked his disciples, “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?” They said some thought John the Baptizer, others Elijah, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.

Then Jesus made it personal: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus said Peter was blessed, because his Father in heaven had revealed this to him.

Jesus told Peter he would build his church on this rock, and “the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.” Christians understand the rock in different ways. Then Jesus told the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ.
Christ means the anointed one: the King God had promised to send. Peter said it out loud. The question Jesus asked his disciples is still the most important one you can answer: who do you say he is?
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

cards.question: Who did people say Jesus might be?
cards.explain: The disciples said, “Some say John the Baptizer, some, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

cards.question: Who did Jesus say had revealed Peter’s answer to him?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.”

cards.text: People had many ideas about Jesus. Peter said: you are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus asks you too.

lessons.title: On the mountain
lessons.prayer: Father, Jesus is your beloved Son. Help me listen to him today above every other voice.

cards.text: After six days, Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain by themselves. There he was changed before them. “His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.”

Moses and Elijah appeared, talking with Jesus. Peter offered to make three tents. While he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”

The disciples fell on their faces, very afraid. Jesus came, touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid.” The same Jesus who shone like the sun came close to lift them up. He comes close to you too.
While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”

cards.question: Who appeared on the mountain, talking with Jesus?
cards.explain: Matthew says, “Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.” Moses brought God’s law to Israel, and Elijah was a great prophet.

cards.question: On the way down, Jesus told them to tell everyone right away what they had seen.
cards.explain: Jesus said, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”

cards.text: On the mountain Jesus shone with glory, and the Father said: this is my beloved Son. Listen to him.

lessons.title: Lazarus, come out
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you are the resurrection and the life. Thank you that you care about my sorrow and give me hope.

cards.text: Lazarus of Bethany was sick, and his sisters, Martha and Mary, sent word to Jesus. He said the sickness was “for the glory of God”. John says Jesus loved all three, yet he stayed two more days where he was.

By the time Jesus came, Lazarus had died. Martha told him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.” Jesus didn’t scold her. He answered with a promise. You can bring him your honest hurt too.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies. Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
Mary came and fell at Jesus’ feet, weeping. When he saw her and the others weeping, he was deeply troubled. He asked where Lazarus had been laid. Then John says simply, “Jesus wept.”

At the tomb, a cave with a stone against it, Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha warned that he had been dead four days. Jesus thanked his Father, then cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” And the dead man came out, still bound in wrappings.

cards.question: How long had Lazarus been dead when Jesus came to the tomb?
cards.explain: At the tomb Martha said, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”

cards.question: When Jesus saw Mary and those with her weeping, he wept too.
cards.explain: John says Jesus “groaned in the spirit and was troubled”, and then, “Jesus wept.”

cards.text: Jesus wept with his friends, then called Lazarus out of the tomb. He is the resurrection and the life.

lessons.title: Zacchaeus
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for seeking me and calling me by name. Change my heart the way you changed Zacchaeus.

cards.text: Jesus was passing through Jericho. A rich chief tax collector named Zacchaeus wanted to see who Jesus was, but he was short and the crowd was in the way. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree.

Jesus looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.” He came down joyfully, while the crowd grumbled. Then Zacchaeus promised half his goods to the poor and to repay four times anything he had wrongly taken.
The crowd saw only a sinner. Jesus called him a son of Abraham and said salvation had come to his house. However far you feel from God, Jesus came “to seek and to save that which was lost.”
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.

cards.question: Why did Zacchaeus climb a tree?
choices: He was short and couldn’t see Jesus
He was hiding from the crowd
He wanted to pick its fruit
cards.answer: He was short and couldn’t see Jesus
cards.explain: Luke says he couldn’t see Jesus “because of the crowd, because he was short”, so he climbed a sycamore tree.

cards.question: How much did Zacchaeus promise to pay back anyone he had cheated?
cards.explain: Zacchaeus said, “If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”

cards.text: Jesus called Zacchaeus by name and stayed at his house. Love came first, and a changed life followed.

lessons.title: A king on a donkey
lessons.prayer: Jesus, my humble King, you came gently. I welcome you into my heart and my day. Hosanna!

cards.text: Near Jerusalem, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples into a village. He said they would find a donkey tied there with her colt, and to bring them to him. If anyone asked, they were to say, “The Lord needs them.”

They laid their clothes on the donkey and the colt, and Jesus sat on them. A huge crowd spread clothes and branches on the road, shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David!” The whole city was stirred, asking, “Who is this?”
Matthew says this fulfilled the prophet’s words: “your King comes to you, humble, and riding on a donkey”. Jesus is a King, but a humble one, and he still comes to you gently.
The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

cards.question: What animals did the disciples bring to Jesus?
cards.explain: Jesus said they would find “a donkey tied, and a colt with her”, and the disciples brought them both.

cards.question: When the city asked who Jesus was, what did the crowds answer?
cards.explain: The crowds said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”

cards.text: Jesus rode into Jerusalem as a humble King, to shouts of Hosanna. Christians remember this day on Palm Sunday.

lessons.title: The last supper
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for giving yourself for me. Teach me to love and serve others the way you served your friends.

cards.text: At Passover, the feast that remembers how God freed Israel from Egypt, Jesus sat at the table with the 12 apostles. He told them, “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.”

He took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.” After supper he took the cup: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.”
John’s Gospel tells how, during supper, Jesus got up, wrapped a towel around his waist and began to wash his disciples’ feet, a servant’s job. Peter protested, “You will never wash my feet!”
That night the disciples argued over who was the greatest. Jesus said, “I am among you as one who serves.” In his Kingdom, greatness looks like serving others, and he went first.
He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”

cards.question: What did the disciples argue about at the supper?
choices: Which of them was the greatest
Who would pay for the food
cards.answer: Which of them was the greatest
cards.explain: Luke says, “A dispute also arose among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.”

cards.question: Peter was glad to let Jesus wash his feet right away.
cards.explain: Peter first said, “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus answered, “If I don’t wash you, you have no part with me.”

cards.text: At his last supper Jesus shared bread and cup and washed his friends’ feet. Christians remember it in Communion, the Lord’s Supper or Eucharist.

lessons.title: Gethsemane
lessons.prayer: Father, when I am overwhelmed, help me pray like Jesus did: not what I want, but what you want.

cards.text: Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane. Taking Peter, James and John with him, he said, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death.” Then he went a little farther, fell on his face and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me”.

Three times Jesus prayed, and each time he came back to find his friends asleep. He said to Peter, “The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” Then he said the hour had come for the Son of Man to be betrayed.

Judas, one of the 12, arrived with a crowd armed with swords and clubs. He greeted Jesus with a kiss, the sign he had given them, and they seized Jesus. When one of Jesus’ friends struck with a sword, Jesus said, “Put your sword back into its place.”

Jesus didn’t hide his anguish. He told his friends how heavy his soul was, and he told his Father. Then he trusted him: “not what I desire, but what you desire.” You can bring God your honest fear too.
He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”

cards.question: How did Judas show the crowd which man was Jesus?
cards.explain: Judas had told them, “Whoever I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.” Then he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.

cards.question: When Jesus was arrested, his disciples stayed by his side.
cards.explain: Matthew says, “Then all the disciples left him and fled.”

cards.text: In the garden Jesus prayed through deep sorrow and chose his Father’s will, even as his friends slept and then fled.

lessons.title: The cross
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for giving your life on the cross. Remember me, and help me forgive others as you forgave.

cards.text: As Jesus was led away, a man named Simon of Cyrene was made to carry the cross behind him. A great crowd followed, with women mourning. At the place called The Skull, they crucified Jesus between two criminals.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.

One criminal insulted Jesus. The other said Jesus had done nothing wrong and asked, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.” Jesus answered, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

From about the sixth hour to the ninth, about noon to three, darkness came over the land, and the veil of the temple was torn in two. Jesus cried, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” and breathed his last. A centurion said, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”

Why the cross? Paul passed on what he had received: “Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures.” Christians understand the cross as the greatest act of love: Jesus gave his life so you could be forgiven.

cards.question: Who was made to carry the cross behind Jesus?
cards.explain: Luke says they grabbed “one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid the cross on him to carry it after Jesus.”

cards.question: What did Jesus promise the criminal who asked to be remembered?
choices: Today you will be with me in Paradise
You will come down from the cross alive
You must pay for your crimes first
cards.answer: Today you will be with me in Paradise
cards.explain: Jesus said to him, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

cards.text: On the cross Jesus prayed for others to be forgiven, promised Paradise to a dying man and gave his spirit to the Father.

lessons.title: He is risen
lessons.prayer: Risen Jesus, thank you that you know my name. Help me live today in the hope of your empty tomb.

cards.text: On the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene found the stone taken away from the tomb. She ran to tell Peter and the other disciple. They ran to the tomb and found the linen cloths lying there. The other disciple “saw and believed.”

Mary stood outside the tomb, weeping. She saw two angels in white where Jesus’ body had lain. Then she turned and saw Jesus standing there, but she didn’t know it was him. She thought he was the gardener.
Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said, “Rabboni!” which means Teacher. He sent her to his brothers, and Mary Magdalene told the disciples that she had seen the Lord.

The good news doesn’t end at the cross. Paul wrote that Christ died, “was buried,” and “was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.” Christians understand the empty tomb as the sign that death doesn’t get the last word.
Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!”

cards.question: Who came to the tomb while it was still dark and found the stone taken away?
cards.explain: John says “Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw that the stone had been taken away”.

cards.question: Who did Mary think Jesus was at first?
cards.explain: John says she was “supposing him to be the gardener”, until Jesus said her name.

cards.text: The tomb was empty. Jesus is risen, and he called Mary by name. He knows your name too.

lessons.title: Go and make disciples
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for being with me always. Give me courage to share your love wherever I go.

cards.text: The 11 disciples went to the mountain in Galilee where Jesus had sent them. They saw him and bowed down, though some doubted. Jesus said, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth,” and sent them to make disciples of all nations.
Even with some doubts among them, Jesus gave his friends his mission and his promise: “I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Wherever you go, you don’t go alone.

In Acts, the disciples asked if Jesus would now restore the kingdom to Israel. He said it wasn’t for them to know the times the Father had set. But they would receive power when the Holy Spirit came, and be his witnesses to the uttermost parts of the earth.

As they watched, he was taken up, and a cloud hid him from their sight. Two men in white asked why they stood looking into the sky. This Jesus, they said, “will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.” Christians call this the Ascension.

“Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

cards.question: What did Jesus say the disciples would receive when the Holy Spirit came?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” Then they would be his witnesses.

cards.question: Who did Jesus send his followers to make disciples of?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “Go and make disciples of all nations”, baptizing them and teaching them all he had commanded.

cards.text: Jesus sent his followers into all the world with the Spirit’s power and a promise that he is with them always.

paths.title: The Big Story of the Bible
paths.subtitle: From the garden to the new creation: how the whole Bible fits together.

lessons.title: In the beginning
lessons.prayer: God, you made everything and saw that it was very good. Thank you for making me in your image.

cards.text: The Bible’s first line is “In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.” The earth was formless and empty, and darkness covered the deep. Then God spoke: “Let there be light,” and there was light.
Then God made people, male and female, in his own image. He blessed them and put them in charge of the fish, the birds and every living thing on the earth.
God made you on purpose. Every person you meet carries his image, and so do you. Your worth starts with who made you, not with what you do.
God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

cards.question: At the end of the sixth day, God looked at everything he had made. What did he see?
cards.explain: Genesis 1:31 says God saw everything he had made, “and, behold, it was very good.”

cards.question: On the seventh day, God rested from his work and blessed the day.
cards.explain: Genesis 2:2-3 says he “rested on the seventh day from all his work” and blessed the day and made it holy.

cards.text: God made a very good world and put his image on people. Next, that good world is broken when people turn from him.

lessons.title: The garden and the fall
lessons.prayer: God, when I want to hide from you, help me hear you calling me. Thank you for coming to find me.

cards.text: God put the first man in the garden of Eden to tend it. He could eat from every tree but one: the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

A serpent told the woman, “You won’t really die.” She ate the fruit and gave some to her husband, and he ate too. Their eyes were opened, and when they heard God in the garden, they hid among the trees.
The LORD God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

Even as God judged the serpent, he made a promise: the woman’s offspring “will bruise your head.” Christians have long read this as the first hint of a rescuer, and the rest of the Bible follows that thread.

cards.question: What did God make for Adam and his wife before sending them out of the garden?
cards.explain: They had sewn fig leaves for themselves, but Genesis 3:21 says the LORD God “made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.”

cards.question: The serpent told the woman she would surely die if she ate the fruit.
cards.explain: The serpent said the opposite: “You won’t really die.” He twisted what God had said.

cards.text: Sin broke the very good world, but God came looking and spoke of hope. Next, as evil spreads, God saves one family.

lessons.title: Noah and the promise
lessons.prayer: God, thank you that you keep your promises. When I see a rainbow, remind me that your word holds.

cards.text: The LORD saw how great human evil had become on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart. He decided to wipe out life from the earth. “But Noah found favor in the LORD’s eyes.”
God told Noah a flood was coming and to build a huge ship, the ark. Noah, his family and two of every kind of living thing would go inside and be kept alive.

cards.question: When the flood covered the earth, who was left alive?
choices: Noah and those with him in the ship
cards.answer: Noah and those with him in the ship
cards.explain: Genesis 7:23 says, “Only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ship.”

cards.question: As the waters went down, what did the dove bring back to Noah?
cards.explain: Genesis 8:11 says the dove came back with “a freshly plucked olive leaf” in her mouth, so Noah knew the waters were going down.

cards.text: After the flood God made a covenant, a binding promise: “There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.” The rainbow is its sign. God ties himself to his word, and you can lean your weight on it.
I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
God judged evil but saved Noah and bound himself to a promise. Next, he promises one man a blessing for every family on earth.

lessons.title: A promise to Abraham
lessons.prayer: God, help me trust your promises before I can see how they come true, the way Abraham did.

cards.text: God told a man named Abram to leave his country and his father’s house for a land God would show him. He promised to make him a great nation, and said, “All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”

So Abram went, at 75 years old, with his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot. When they reached the land of Canaan, God appeared to him and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” Abram built an altar there.

Later, Abram still had no child. God told him to count the stars: “So your offspring will be.” Abram had nothing but God’s word, and he believed it. God counted that trust as righteousness, and you can lean on his word too.
I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.

cards.question: God said that through Abram, who would be blessed?
choices: All the families of the earth
cards.answer: All the families of the earth
cards.explain: God promised, “All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.” The plan was always bigger than one family.

cards.question: What new name did God later give Abram?
cards.explain: In Genesis 17:5 God said, “your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.”

cards.text: God promised Abram a family, a land and a blessing for the whole world. Next, his family grows into a people, but ends up enslaved in Egypt.

lessons.title: Out of Egypt
lessons.prayer: God, you heard your people’s cry and made a way through the sea. When I feel trapped, help me trust you.

cards.text: Abraham’s descendants were now a people, suffering under cruel taskmasters in Egypt. God spoke to Moses from a bush that burned but didn’t burn up: “I have surely seen the affliction of my people.” He had come down to rescue them.

God told Israel’s families to kill a lamb and put its blood on their doorposts. That night he would strike the firstborn of Egypt, but “When I see the blood, I will pass over you.” It was the LORD’s Passover.
Moses stretched out his hand, and the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind. Israel crossed on dry ground. Pharaoh’s army went in after them, and the waters came back and covered them.

With the sea ahead and chariots behind, the people were terrified. Moses said, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.” They couldn’t save themselves, and they didn’t have to. You can bring your dead ends to the same God.
The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.

cards.question: At the first Passover, what did each household put on its doorposts?
cards.explain: God told each household to take a lamb and put “some of the blood” on the two door posts and the lintel of the house.

cards.question: How did the children of Israel cross the sea?
cards.explain: Exodus 14:22 says they went into the middle of the sea “on the dry ground,” with the waters like a wall on each side.

cards.text: God heard his people’s cry, spared them at Passover and opened the sea. Next, at Mount Sinai, he shows his rescued people how to live.

lessons.title: The law at Sinai
lessons.prayer: God, you loved me before I kept a single rule. Help me live your way because I’m yours.

cards.text: In the third month after leaving Egypt, Israel camped at Mount Sinai. God reminded them, “I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself,” and invited them to be his own people, “a holy nation.”
On the third day the mountain shook. There was thunder, lightning, a thick cloud and a very loud trumpet, and Mount Sinai smoked because the LORD came down on it in fire. The people trembled.

Before a single command, God said who he was: the one who brought them out of slavery. The rescue came first, then the rules. The commandments weren’t a way to earn their rescue but a way for a freed people to live. God’s love comes first for you too.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

cards.question: Which of these is one of the Ten Commandments?
choices: Honor your father and your mother
Give away half of what you own
cards.answer: Honor your father and your mother
cards.explain: Exodus 20:12 says, “Honor your father and your mother.” The commands right after it protect life, marriage, property and the truth.

cards.question: Frightened by the thunder and smoke, the people asked Moses to speak to them instead of God.
cards.explain: They said, “Speak with us yourself, and we will listen; but don’t let God speak with us, lest we die.”

cards.text: God rescued his people first, then gave them his law. Next, in the promised land, God chooses a shepherd boy named David to be king.

lessons.title: King David
lessons.prayer: God, thank you that you look at the heart. When I feel overlooked, remind me that you see me.

cards.text: God had rejected Saul as king and sent Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint a new king from the sons of Jesse. Samuel saw Jesse’s son Eliab and was sure he was the one. But God told him not to judge by looks or height.

But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”

Seven of Jesse’s sons passed by, and God chose none of them. The youngest was out keeping the sheep. When he came in, God said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.” Samuel anointed him, and the Spirit of the LORD came mightily on David.
Jesse didn’t even call David in at first. He was the youngest, out with the sheep, and he was God’s choice. Being overlooked by people doesn’t mean being overlooked by God.
Later, God gave King David a promise through Nathan: one of David’s offspring would reign after him, and God would “establish the throne of his kingdom forever.”

cards.question: What did Samuel use to anoint David?
cards.explain: 1 Samuel 16:13 says Samuel “took the horn of oil and anointed him in the middle of his brothers.”

cards.question: God promised that David’s throne would be established forever.
cards.explain: Through Nathan, God told David, “Your throne will be established forever.”

cards.text: God chose David for his heart and promised his throne would last forever. Next, the prophets point ahead to a greater king.

lessons.title: The prophets
lessons.prayer: God, thank you for speaking through your prophets. Help me act justly, love mercy and walk humbly with you.

cards.text: God sent prophets to speak for him and call his people back. Through Micah, someone asks how to please God: burnt offerings? Thousands of rams? The answer: “to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God.”
Isaiah spoke of a great light for people in darkness, and a child born to reign “on David’s throne,” with peace that would have no end. The promise to David was still alive.

The book of Isaiah also speaks of one who suffers for others: “he was pierced for our transgressions,” and “the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.” Christians understand this as pointing to Jesus and his death on the cross.
Through Jeremiah, God promised a new covenant. He would write his law on hearts and “remember their sin no more.” Christians believe that promise reaches you: forgiven, and changed from the inside.
For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

cards.question: According to Micah, what does the LORD require of you?
choices: Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly
Thousands of rams on the altar
cards.answer: Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly
cards.explain: Micah 6:8 says the LORD requires you “to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God.”

cards.question: In the new covenant, where did God say he would write his law?
cards.explain: God said, “I will put my law in their inward parts, and I will write it in their heart.”

cards.text: The prophets called God’s people back and pointed ahead to a coming king. Next, God’s people lose their home and wait to return.

lessons.title: Exile and coming home
lessons.prayer: God, in seasons of waiting, help me seek you with all my heart and trust that you are with me there.

cards.text: Then the worst happened. Babylon’s army burned the temple and the great houses of Jerusalem, broke down the city walls and carried the people of the city away captive.

Years before the city fell, after the first captives were taken, the prophet Jeremiah sent them a letter from Jerusalem. God told them to build houses, plant gardens and raise families in Babylon, and to “Seek the peace of the city” and pray for it.

God’s promise of “hope and a future” was first spoken to captives far from home, facing a long wait. He didn’t skip the wait. He promised, “You shall seek me and find me.” If you’re waiting too, you can seek him there.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, God stirred his heart, and Cyrus let the captives go home to rebuild the LORD’s house in Jerusalem. The book of Ezra says it happened so the word spoken by Jeremiah would be fulfilled.
“For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says the LORD, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.”

cards.question: What did God tell the captives to do in Babylon?
choices: Refuse to pray for the city
cards.explain: God told them, “Build houses and dwell in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.” He even told them to pray for the city.

cards.question: After how many years did God promise to bring the captives back?
cards.explain: God said, “After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon, I will visit you,” and promised to bring them back to this place.

cards.text: God’s people lost their home, but God kept his word and brought them back. Next, the greatest promise of all comes true in Jesus.

lessons.title: Jesus, the promise kept
lessons.prayer: Jesus, open my eyes to see you in all the Scriptures, and walk with me on my road today.

cards.text: Then the promise arrived. Paul writes that “when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law.” He came so “that we might receive the adoption as children.”

John’s Gospel says, “The Word became flesh and lived among us.” Christians understand the Word to be Jesus: God not sending a message from far away but coming close, “full of grace and truth.” That is how near he wants to be to you.
After the crucifixion, two of Jesus’ followers walked to a village called Emmaus, sad and talking it all over. Jesus himself came and walked with them, but they didn’t recognize him.
Jesus called them “slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken,” and asked, “Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

cards.question: When did the two followers finally recognize Jesus?
choices: When he called them by name
cards.explain: Luke 24:35 says he “was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.”

cards.question: Jesus said the law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms all wrote about him.
cards.explain: He said “all things which are written in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms concerning me must be fulfilled.”

cards.text: From Moses to the prophets, every promise pointed to Jesus, and he is risen. Next, he sends the promised Spirit and the church is born.

lessons.title: The church is born
lessons.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank you that the promise is for me too. Help me love and share like the first believers did.

cards.text: On the day of Pentecost, Jesus’ followers were together in one place. A sound like a mighty rushing wind filled the house, tongues like fire rested on each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit.
Jews from every nation were staying in Jerusalem. Each one heard these Galileans speaking in his own language about “the mighty works of God.” Amazed, they asked, “What does this mean?”

Peter told the crowd that God had made Jesus, the one they crucified, “both Lord and Christ.” Cut to the heart, they asked what to do. Peter told them to repent and be baptized in Jesus’ name, and about 3,000 people were added that day.

Peter said, “the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are far off.” The Spirit wasn’t only for one crowd in Jerusalem. The promise keeps going out to people far off, and that includes you.
They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.

cards.question: Why was the crowd that gathered so bewildered?
choices: Each heard them in his own language
They saw Jesus in the sky
cards.answer: Each heard them in his own language
cards.explain: Acts 2:6 says they were bewildered “because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.”

cards.question: What did the first believers do with their possessions?
cards.explain: Acts 2:45 says they sold their possessions and goods and “distributed them to all, according as anyone had need.”

cards.text: The Spirit came and the good news began going out to every nation. Last comes the ending: God making all things new.

lessons.title: All things new
lessons.prayer: God, thank you that every tear is seen and the story ends with you. Fill me with hope for what you are making new.

cards.text: The Bible began with God making the heavens and the earth. It ends with John’s vision of “a new heaven and a new earth,” and the holy city, New Jerusalem, “coming down out of heaven from God.”

A loud voice announced, “God’s dwelling is with people.” He will wipe away every tear, and death, mourning and pain will be gone. Whatever you carry today, the story ends with God close and every tear wiped away.
He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”
John was shown a river of the water of life flowing from God’s throne, and beside it the tree of life, with leaves “for the healing of the nations.” And “There will be no curse any more.”

cards.question: What did John see coming down out of heaven from God?
cards.explain: Revelation 21:2 says he saw “the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God.”

cards.question: In John’s vision, God wipes away every tear and death is no more.
cards.explain: Revelation 21:4 says, “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more.”

cards.text: The curse from the garden is gone and the tree of life is open again. The whole Bible is one story: God making his home with his people.

paths.title: Parables of Jesus
paths.subtitle: The short stories Jesus told, and what they show about God.

lessons.title: The sower
lessons.prayer: Jesus, make my heart good soil. Clear away the worries that crowd out your word, and let it grow in me.

cards.text: Jesus sat in a boat and taught the crowd on the shore in parables. A farmer went out to sow. Some seed fell on the path and birds ate it, some on rocky ground and withered, some among thorns and was choked. Some fell on good soil and gave a great crop.

Later Jesus explained it. The seed is the word of the Kingdom. The path is hearing without understanding. Rocky ground is joy with no root. Thorns are worries and riches choking the word. Good soil hears, understands and bears fruit.
You may see yourself in more than one soil. Jesus names what can crowd out God’s word, the cares of this age and the pull of riches, so you can notice them and give his word room to grow.
What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.

cards.question: In Jesus’ explanation, what chokes the word among the thorns?
choices: Worries and the deceitfulness of riches
Birds that come and snatch it
cards.answer: Worries and the deceitfulness of riches
cards.explain: Matthew 13:22 says “the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word.”

cards.question: In the story, the seed on rocky ground never sprouted.
cards.explain: It sprang up quickly, but when the sun rose it was scorched. “Because they had no root, they withered away.”

cards.text: The same seed lands everywhere. What matters is the soil: hearing God’s word, understanding it and letting it bear fruit.

lessons.title: The mustard seed and the yeast
lessons.prayer: God, when your work in me looks small, help me trust that you are growing something good.

cards.text: Jesus said the Kingdom of Heaven is like a mustard seed a man planted in his field. It is tiny, smaller than all seeds, but it grows into a tree, and the birds come and rest in its branches.
Then he said it is like yeast a woman mixed into three measures of flour. A little yeast, hidden in the dough, worked through the whole batch.

To those first listeners, God’s kingdom may not have looked like much: no army, no palace, just Jesus and his followers. Christians often read these stories as a promise that it starts small and hidden but grows to fill everything.
He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”

cards.question: What did the tiny mustard seed grow into?
choices: A small bush that dried up
cards.explain: Jesus said it “becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”

cards.question: In the parable, the yeast worked through only part of the dough.
cards.explain: Jesus said the yeast was hidden in three measures of meal “until it was all leavened.”

cards.text: God’s kingdom often starts small and hidden. What looks tiny in your life can be where he is growing something.

lessons.title: The treasure and the pearl
lessons.prayer: Jesus, you are worth more than anything I could hold onto. Give me the joy of the man who found the treasure.

cards.text: Jesus told two very short stories. A man found treasure hidden in a field, hid it again, and in his joy sold everything he had to buy that field. A merchant looking for fine pearls found one of great value and sold all that he had to buy it.
The man gives up everything, and he does it “In his joy.” Jesus isn’t describing a grim sacrifice but a find so good that nothing else compares. That is how much he says God’s kingdom is worth.
Christians read these stories in more than one way. Many see God’s kingdom as the treasure worth everything you have. Others also see Jesus as the one who gave everything to make people his own.
Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.

cards.question: What did the man do after he found the treasure?
choices: Sold all he had and bought the field
Dug it up and ran away
Told the owner and left it
cards.answer: Sold all he had and bought the field
cards.explain: Matthew 13:44 says “In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.”

cards.question: What was the merchant searching for?
cards.explain: Jesus said the kingdom is like “a merchant seeking fine pearls,” who sold all he had for one.

cards.text: God’s kingdom is the find of a lifetime, worth more than everything else, and finding it brings joy.

lessons.title: The lost sheep and the lost coin
lessons.prayer: Jesus, thank you for coming after me when I wander, and for the joy in heaven when anyone comes home.

cards.text: Tax collectors and sinners were crowding around to hear Jesus. Tax collectors were widely despised in his day. The Pharisees and scribes grumbled, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.” So Jesus told them a story.

Jesus asked: if you had 100 sheep and lost one, wouldn’t you leave the 99 and search until you found it, then carry it home rejoicing? Or if a woman lost one of her 10 silver coins, she would light a lamp and sweep until she found it, then call her friends to celebrate.

Jesus spells out the point: there is joy in heaven “over one sinner who repents.” The religious leaders grumbled about who Jesus welcomed, but heaven celebrates them. If you feel far away, notice who does the searching.
Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.

cards.question: In Luke 15, why were the Pharisees and scribes grumbling?
choices: Jesus welcomed and ate with sinners
cards.answer: Jesus welcomed and ate with sinners
cards.explain: Luke 15:2 says they murmured, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”

cards.question: What did the woman do to find her lost coin?
choices: Lit a lamp and swept the house
Waited for it to turn up
cards.answer: Lit a lamp and swept the house
cards.explain: Jesus said she would “light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it.”

cards.text: Jesus welcomes the lost and goes looking for them, and heaven rejoices when one comes home.

lessons.title: The lost son
lessons.prayer: Father, thank you for running to meet me. Whether I’ve wandered off or stayed and grown cold, bring me into your joy.

cards.text: A man had two sons. The younger asked for his share of the property, went off to a far country and wasted it all on wild living. When famine struck, he ended up feeding pigs, so hungry he wanted their food.

He came to his senses and headed home to ask to be a hired servant. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, ran to him and kissed him. He called for the best robe, a ring and a feast: “He was lost and is found.”

The older son came in from the field, heard the party and was angry. He wouldn’t go in. His father came out to him too: “Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.” The story ends without saying what he did.

Jesus told this to grumbling religious leaders, with tax collectors and sinners listening in. Christians often see the grumblers in the older brother. Whichever son you relate to, the father comes out to meet you.
He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.

cards.question: What work did the younger son end up doing in the far country?
cards.explain: Luke 15:15 says a citizen of that country “sent him into his fields to feed pigs.” For Jesus’ Jewish listeners, pigs were unclean animals, so this was rock bottom.

cards.question: The older son happily joined the celebration.
cards.explain: Luke 15:28 says “he was angry and would not go in,” so his father came out and begged him.

cards.text: The father ran to the son who left and went out to the son who stayed. Both were invited into his joy.

lessons.title: The good Samaritan
lessons.prayer: Jesus, open my eyes to the person in front of me who needs mercy, and give me the courage to stop.

cards.text: A lawyer, an expert in God’s law, asked Jesus how to inherit eternal life. Asked what the law said, he answered: love God with all you are, and your neighbor as yourself. Then, wanting to justify himself, he asked, “Who is my neighbor?”

Jesus told of a man robbed, beaten and left half dead on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho. A priest saw him and passed by on the other side, and so did a Levite. Then a Samaritan came, was moved with compassion, bandaged him, took him to an inn and paid for his care.

Samaritans and Jews were at odds in Jesus’ day, so a Samaritan hero would have surprised his listeners. Jesus turned the question from who your neighbor is to whether you act like one. Then he said, “Go and do likewise.”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”

cards.question: Who stopped to help the beaten man?
cards.explain: A priest and a Levite passed by on the other side. A Samaritan “was moved with compassion” and cared for him.

cards.question: What question did the lawyer ask to justify himself?
cards.explain: Luke 10:29 says that, “desiring to justify himself,” he asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”

cards.text: Jesus didn’t list who counts as a neighbor. He showed what a neighbor does: stops, cares and shows mercy.

lessons.title: The two builders
lessons.prayer: Jesus, I don’t want only to hear your words. Help me build my life on them, so I stand when storms come.

cards.text: Jesus said whoever hears his words and does them is like a wise man who built his house on rock. Whoever hears but doesn’t do them is like a foolish man who built on sand. The same rain, floods and wind hit both. One stood. The other fell, “and its fall was great.”

These were the closing words of a long teaching, and the crowds were astonished because Jesus taught “with authority.” He wasn’t offering nice ideas to admire. He was saying his words are the ground to build a life on.
Both houses faced the same storm. Following Jesus doesn’t mean storms skip you. It means there is something solid under you when they come. Hearing is the start; doing is the foundation.
Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.

cards.question: Who does Jesus say is like the wise builder?
choices: Whoever hears his words and does them
Whoever hears his words and agrees
cards.answer: Whoever hears his words and does them
cards.explain: Matthew 7:24 says “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them” is like the wise man who built on the rock.

cards.question: In the story, only the foolish man’s house faced a storm.
cards.explain: The same rain, floods and winds beat on both houses. Only the one “founded on the rock” stood.

cards.text: Hearing Jesus is the start. Doing what he says is the rock that holds when the storms come.

lessons.title: The unforgiving servant
lessons.prayer: Father, you have forgiven me so much. Give me a heart that forgives others, even when it’s hard.

cards.text: Peter asked Jesus how often he had to forgive someone who sinned against him. Seven times? Jesus said, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.”

Then Jesus told of a servant who owed a king 10,000 talents, a fortune he couldn’t pay. He begged, and the king forgave it all. That servant then found a man who owed him 100 denarii, a small sum by comparison, and had him thrown in prison.
Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?
The king expected mercy received to become mercy given. Jesus ends with a serious warning to forgive “from your hearts.” If that feels hard, start by remembering how much you have been forgiven.

cards.question: When Peter suggested forgiving seven times, what did Jesus say?
cards.explain: Jesus said, “until seventy times seven.” Some Bibles read seventy-seven times. Either way, it is far past keeping count.

cards.question: After being forgiven, the servant forgave his fellow servant’s small debt too.
cards.explain: He grabbed the man by the throat, demanded, “Pay me what you owe!” and threw him into prison.

cards.text: In Jesus’ story, the king forgave a debt no one could pay. Jesus asks you to pass mercy on, again and again.

lessons.title: The rich fool
lessons.prayer: God, thank you for every good thing I have. Help me hold it with open hands and be rich toward you.

cards.text: A man in the crowd asked Jesus to make his brother share the family inheritance. Jesus wouldn’t act as judge between them. Instead he warned everyone to watch out for greed, and told a story.

A rich man’s land produced a huge crop. He planned to tear down his barns, build bigger ones, and tell himself to take it easy: “eat, drink, and be merry.” But God said, “You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you.”

The man only talks to himself, about himself. Jesus says the trouble is storing up treasure for yourself while not being “rich toward God.” You can plan and work hard and still ask: what am I storing up, and who is it for?
He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”

cards.question: What did the rich man plan to do with his huge harvest?
choices: Build bigger barns to store it
cards.answer: Build bigger barns to store it
cards.explain: He said, “I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.”

cards.question: Jesus agreed to settle the brothers’ inheritance argument.
cards.explain: Jesus answered, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”

cards.text: Life is more than what you own. The rich fool built bigger barns, but Jesus invites you to be rich toward God.

lessons.title: The Pharisee and the tax collector
lessons.prayer: God, have mercy on me. I come to you honestly, not because I’m better than anyone, but because I need you.

cards.text: Jesus told this story to people who were sure of their own goodness and looked down on everyone else. Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee. The other was a tax collector.

The Pharisee thanked God he wasn’t like other people, “or even like this tax collector,” and listed his fasting and giving. The tax collector stood far off, wouldn’t even look up, beat his chest and prayed, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”

In Jesus’ day, Pharisees were respected for keeping God’s law carefully, and tax collectors were widely despised. Yet Jesus said the tax collector went home justified, right with God. God welcomes the honest prayer of someone who knows they need mercy.
