I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.

cards.question: What did the tax collector pray?
choices: God, be merciful to me, a sinner!
God, I thank you I’m not like others
God, see how often I fast
cards.answer: God, be merciful to me, a sinner!
cards.explain: Luke 18:13 says he beat his chest, saying, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”

cards.question: Jesus said the Pharisee was the one who went home justified.
cards.explain: Jesus said of the tax collector, “this man went down to his house justified rather than the other.”

cards.text: Jesus lifted up the humble prayer, not the proud one. God hears anyone who comes honestly asking for mercy.

lessons.title: The workers in the vineyard
lessons.prayer: God, thank you that your grace isn’t earned by the hour. Help me rejoice when you are generous to others.

cards.text: Jesus said the Kingdom of Heaven is like a landowner who hired workers at dawn for a denarius, a day’s wage. He kept going back to hire more all day long, right up to the eleventh hour, when he found people standing idle because “no one has hired us.”

At evening, everyone got a denarius, starting with those who had worked one hour. The first grumbled that they had worked all day in the heat. The owner said, “Friend, I am doing you no wrong,” and asked if they were envious because he was generous.

Christians often read this as a picture of God’s grace: no one earns it by the hour, and latecomers are welcomed just as fully. If you feel late to faith, you aren’t behind. If you’ve served for years, you get to celebrate his generosity.
So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.

cards.question: What were the workers hired last paid?
cards.explain: Matthew 20:9-10 says those hired at the eleventh hour “each received a denarius,” and so did those hired first.

cards.question: The landowner paid the first workers less than he had promised.
cards.explain: He told them, “Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?” They received exactly what they agreed to.

cards.text: The landowner was fair to the first and generous to the last. Jesus says God’s kingdom is like that.

lessons.title: The talents
lessons.prayer: Lord, thank you for all you’ve put in my hands. Help me use it faithfully instead of burying it out of fear.

cards.text: Before a journey, a man trusted his servants with his money: five talents to one, two to another, one to a third, each by his ability. A talent was a very large sum. The first two put it to work and doubled it. The third dug a hole and hid it.
After a long time the master came back. To each of the first two he said, “Well done, good and faithful servant,” and invited them to “Enter into the joy of your lord.”

The third servant said he was afraid, so he buried what he was given. The master wanted it used, not hidden. Christians often read the talents as whatever God puts in your hands: time, gifts, chances to love.
His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’

cards.question: What did the servant with one talent do with it?
cards.explain: Matthew 25:18 says he “dug in the earth and hid his lord’s money.”

cards.question: The servants given five and two talents heard the very same words of praise.
cards.explain: Both heard, “Well done, good and faithful servant.” The master praised their faithfulness, not the size of the amount.

cards.text: Jesus told this while teaching about his return. What God puts in your hands is meant to be used in faith, not buried out of fear.

daily.question: In the creation story, what did God call the light?
daily.explain: Genesis 1:5 says God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”.

daily.question: Which angel was sent from God to Mary in Nazareth?
daily.explain: Luke 1:26-27: “the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth”, to a virgin named Mary.

daily.question: God rested on the seventh day.
daily.explain: Genesis 2:2 says God finished his work, and “he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.”

daily.question: When asked what to call his newborn son, what did Zacharias write on a tablet?
daily.explain: The relatives wanted to name the baby after his father, but Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” They all marveled.

daily.question: In Genesis 2, what did the LORD God form man from?
daily.explain: Genesis 2:7: God “formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”.

daily.question: Luke says Mary laid baby Jesus in a feeding trough because there was no room for them.
daily.explain: Luke 2:7: Mary “wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.”

daily.question: What was Abel’s work?
daily.explain: Genesis 4:2: “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.”

daily.question: Matthew says the wise men came to Jerusalem from which direction?
daily.explain: Matthew 2:1-2: “wise men from the east came to Jerusalem”, asking where the newborn King of the Jews was, because they had seen his star.

daily.question: How long did Methuselah live?
daily.explain: Genesis 5:27: “All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, then he died.”

daily.question: What gifts did the wise men offer the young child?
daily.explain: Matthew 2:11: they found the child with Mary, worshiped him, and “offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.”

daily.question: Genesis says Enoch walked with God, and then God took him.
daily.explain: Genesis 5:24: “Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.”

daily.question: After the wise men left, where did an angel tell Joseph to take the child and his mother?
daily.explain: Matthew 2:13-14: an angel told Joseph in a dream to “flee into Egypt”, and he left by night with the child and his mother.

daily.question: How long did it rain on the earth in Noah’s flood?
daily.explain: Genesis 7:12: “It rained on the earth forty days and forty nights.”

daily.question: Which elderly prophetess, a widow who worshiped in the temple night and day, gave thanks when Jesus was brought there?
daily.explain: Luke 2:36-38: “Anna, a prophetess” of the tribe of Asher, worshiped in the temple night and day. Coming up “at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord”.

daily.question: What did the dove bring back to Noah in her mouth?
daily.explain: Genesis 8:11 says “in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf”, so Noah knew the waters were going down.

daily.question: When Jesus was 12, his parents found him in the temple after three days.
daily.explain: Luke 2:46: “After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.”

daily.question: What did God set in the cloud as the sign of his covenant with the earth?
daily.explain: Genesis 9:13: “I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.”

daily.question: About how old was Jesus when he began to teach?
daily.explain: Luke 3:23: “Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old”.

daily.question: Why was the place called Babel?
choices: The LORD confused the language there
Its tower fell in a storm
Fire fell from the sky there
daily.answer: The LORD confused the language there
daily.explain: Genesis 11:9: “its name was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth.”

daily.question: What was John the Baptizer’s food?
daily.explain: Matthew 3:4: John wore clothing made of camel’s hair with a leather belt. “His food was locusts and wild honey.”

daily.question: What did Abraham see caught in a thicket by its horns?
daily.explain: Genesis 22:13: Abraham “saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns”, and offered it instead of his son.

daily.question: In which river was Jesus baptized by John?
daily.explain: Mark 1:9: “Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.”

daily.question: What did Jacob give Esau in exchange for his birthright?
daily.explain: Esau came in from the field famished and sold his birthright. Then “Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew” (Genesis 25:34).

daily.question: When the storm hit the boat, Jesus was asleep on a cushion.
daily.explain: Mark 4:37-38: as the waves filled the boat, “He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion”, and the disciples woke him up.

daily.question: For how many pieces of silver was Joseph sold?
daily.explain: Genesis 37:28: Joseph was lifted out of the pit and sold “to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver”, and taken to Egypt.

daily.question: In which town did Jesus turn water into wine?
daily.explain: John 2:9-11: the ruler of the feast tasted “the water now become wine”. “This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee”.

daily.question: When Joseph’s brothers came to Egypt, they recognized him right away.
daily.explain: Genesis 42:8: “Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.”

daily.question: Who brought Simon Peter to Jesus?
daily.explain: John 1:40-42: Andrew “first found his own brother, Simon”, and told him they had found the Messiah. “He brought him to Jesus.”

daily.question: Where did baby Moses’ mother set the papyrus basket?
choices: In the reeds by the river’s bank
daily.answer: In the reeds by the river’s bank
daily.explain: Exodus 2:3: she coated a papyrus basket with tar and pitch, put the child in it, and “laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.”

daily.question: What name did Jesus give James and John, the sons of Zebedee?
daily.explain: Mark 3:17: Jesus called James and John “Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder”.

daily.question: The bush Moses saw on fire burned up completely.
daily.explain: Exodus 3:2: “the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.”

daily.question: How did four people get a paralyzed man to Jesus past the crowd?
choices: They carried him in a boat
They let him down through the roof
daily.answer: They let him down through the roof
daily.explain: Mark 2:3-4: they couldn’t come near for the crowd, so “they removed the roof where he was” and let down the mat he was lying on.

daily.question: When Moses threw his rod on the ground, what did it become?
daily.explain: Exodus 4:3: “He threw it on the ground, and it became a snake; and Moses ran away from it.”

daily.question: When did Nicodemus come to see Jesus in John 3?
daily.explain: John 3:1-2: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, “came to Jesus by night” and called him a teacher who has come from God.

daily.question: What did the LORD use to push the sea back all night?
daily.explain: Exodus 14:21: “the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land”.

daily.question: When Jesus asked the man with an unclean spirit, “What is your name?”, what was the answer?
daily.explain: Mark 5:9: “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

daily.question: Moses was older than Aaron.
daily.explain: Exodus 7:7: “Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.”

daily.question: How old was Jairus’ daughter when Jesus raised her?
daily.explain: Mark 5:42: “Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old.”

daily.question: What did manna taste like?
daily.explain: Exodus 16:31: manna “was like coriander seed, white; and its taste was like wafers with honey.”

daily.question: After Jesus fed 5,000 men, how many baskets of leftovers were gathered?
daily.explain: Mark 6:43-44: “They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish. Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.”

daily.question: During the battle with Amalek, who held up Moses’ hands?
daily.explain: Exodus 17:12: Moses’ hands grew heavy, so “Aaron and Hur held up his hands”, one on each side, until sunset.

daily.question: Why did Peter begin to sink when he walked on the water?
choices: He saw the strong wind and was afraid
daily.answer: He saw the strong wind and was afraid
daily.explain: Peter walked on the water to Jesus, but “when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid”. Sinking, he cried out, “Lord, save me!”

daily.question: What did Moses make and set on a pole, so that people bitten by snakes could look at it and live?
daily.explain: Numbers 21:9: “Moses made a serpent of bronze, and set it on the pole.” Anyone who had been bitten looked at it and lived.

daily.question: All ten men healed of leprosy came back to thank Jesus.
daily.explain: Luke 17:15-17: one turned back, glorifying God, “and he was a Samaritan.” Jesus asked, “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?”

daily.question: How old was Moses when he died?
daily.explain: Deuteronomy 34:7: “Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died. His eye was not dim, nor his strength gone.”

daily.question: Which two men appeared, talking with Jesus, on the high mountain?
daily.explain: Matthew 17:1-3: Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain. His face shone like the sun, and “Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.”

daily.question: What did the spies tell Rahab to tie in her window?
daily.explain: Joshua 2:18: “tie this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down”, and gather your family into the house.

daily.question: How long had the man by the pool been sick when Jesus told him to take up his mat and walk?
daily.explain: John 5:5: “A certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.” Jesus said, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.”

daily.question: When did the Jordan stop flowing so Israel could cross?
choices: When the priests’ feet touched the water
daily.answer: When the priests’ feet touched the water
daily.explain: Joshua 3:15-16: when the feet of the priests carrying the ark “dipped in the edge of the water”, the water from upstream stood and rose up in one heap.

daily.question: Jesus told Peter he would find a coin in the mouth of a fish.
daily.explain: Matthew 17:27: “take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin.”

daily.question: On the seventh day, Israel marched around Jericho just once.
daily.explain: Joshua 6:15: on the seventh day they rose at dawn and “marched around the city in the same way seven times.”

daily.question: Where did Jesus send the blind man to wash?
daily.explain: John 9:7: Jesus told him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam”. “So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.”

daily.question: What did Gideon put on the threshing floor to ask God for a sign?
daily.explain: Judges 6:37-38: Gideon put “a fleece of wool on the threshing floor”. The next morning he wrung a bowl full of dew out of it.

daily.question: How many days had Lazarus been in the tomb when Jesus arrived?
daily.explain: John 11:17: “when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.”

daily.question: With how many men did the LORD say he would save Israel through Gideon?
daily.explain: Judges 7:7: “I will save you by the three hundred men who lapped, and deliver the Midianites into your hand.”

daily.question: Why did Zacchaeus climb a tree?
choices: He was short and wanted to see Jesus
He was hiding from the crowd
daily.answer: He was short and wanted to see Jesus
daily.explain: Luke 19:3-4: he couldn’t see Jesus “because of the crowd, because he was short”, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree.

daily.question: Deborah was a prophetess who judged Israel.
daily.explain: Judges 4:4: “Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time.”

daily.question: In Jesus’ story, who stopped to help the man beaten by robbers on the road to Jericho?
daily.explain: Luke 10:31-34: a priest and a Levite passed by on the other side, but “a certain Samaritan” was moved with compassion and took care of him.

daily.question: What did Samson say had never come on his head?
daily.explain: Judges 16:17: “No razor has ever come on my head; for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb.”

daily.question: In the story of the lost son, what job did the younger son end up doing?
daily.explain: Luke 15:15-16: after he spent everything, a citizen “sent him into his fields to feed pigs.” He longed to eat the pods the pigs ate.

daily.question: Ruth and Orpah were women of which land?
daily.explain: Ruth 1:4: Naomi’s sons “took for themselves wives of the women of Moab.” One was Orpah and the other was Ruth.

daily.question: In Jesus’ story, a man with 100 sheep loses one. How many does he leave to go after it?
daily.explain: Luke 15:4: he would “leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it”.

daily.question: Ruth’s son Obed became the grandfather of which king?
daily.explain: Ruth 4:17: “They named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.”

daily.question: In Jesus’ teaching, the wise man built his house on the sand.
daily.explain: Matthew 7:24: whoever hears Jesus’ words and does them is like “a wise man who built his house on the rock.”

daily.question: When the LORD called young Samuel, who did Samuel think was calling him?
daily.explain: 1 Samuel 3:5: Samuel ran to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” Eli said he hadn’t called.

daily.question: Jesus said it is easier for what to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter God’s Kingdom?
daily.explain: Matthew 19:24: “it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”

daily.question: Saul was shorter than most people in Israel.
daily.explain: 1 Samuel 9:2: “From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.”

daily.question: How many pieces of silver did the chief priests weigh out for Judas?
daily.explain: Matthew 26:15: Judas asked what they would give him, and “they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.”

daily.question: What was David doing when Samuel came to anoint one of Jesse’s sons?
daily.explain: 1 Samuel 16:11: Jesse said, “There remains yet the youngest. Behold, he is keeping the sheep.” Samuel sent for him and anointed him.

daily.question: What was the name of the high priest’s servant whose ear Peter cut off?
daily.explain: John 18:10: Simon Peter drew a sword and cut off the servant’s right ear. “The servant’s name was Malchus.”

daily.question: How many smooth stones did David choose from the brook?
daily.explain: 1 Samuel 17:40: David “chose for himself five smooth stones out of the brook” and went toward the Philistine with his sling in his hand.

daily.question: When Jesus died, the veil of the temple tore from the bottom to the top.
daily.explain: Matthew 27:51: “the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.”

daily.question: Who loved David “as his own soul”?
daily.explain: 1 Samuel 18:1: “the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.”

daily.question: In how many languages was the title on Jesus’ cross written?
daily.explain: John 19:19-20: the title Pilate wrote said “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS”, and “it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.”

daily.question: David showed kindness to Mephibosheth for whose sake?
daily.explain: 2 Samuel 9:7: David said, “I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake”, and Mephibosheth would always eat at his table.

daily.question: After the angel rolled the stone away from the tomb, what did he do?
daily.explain: Matthew 28:2: “an angel of the Lord descended from the sky and came and rolled away the stone from the door and sat on it.”

daily.question: David danced before the LORD with all his might.
daily.explain: 2 Samuel 6:14: “David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.”

daily.question: At the tomb, who did Mary Magdalene at first suppose Jesus was?
daily.explain: John 20:14-15: she saw Jesus standing but didn’t know it was him. “She, supposing him to be the gardener,” asked where he had laid the body.

daily.question: When God told Solomon, “Ask for what I should give you”, what did he ask for?
daily.explain: 1 Kings 3:9: “Give your servant therefore an understanding heart to judge your people, that I may discern between good and evil”.

daily.question: On the road to Emmaus, the two disciples knew Jesus as soon as he joined them.
daily.explain: Luke 24:15-16: Jesus himself came near and went with them. “But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.”

daily.question: Solomon finished building the temple in a single year.
daily.explain: 1 Kings 6:38: the house was finished in all its parts, and “he spent seven years building it.”

daily.question: How many large fish were in the net that Peter drew to land?
daily.explain: John 21:11: the net was “full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.”

daily.question: Who brought Elijah bread and meat by the brook, morning and evening?
daily.explain: 1 Kings 17:6: “The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.”

daily.question: Acts says the risen Jesus appeared to the apostles over a period of how many days?
daily.explain: Acts 1:3: he “showed himself alive after he suffered, by many proofs, appearing to them over a period of forty days”.

daily.question: On which mountain did Elijah gather Israel and the prophets of Baal?
daily.explain: 1 Kings 18:19-20: Elijah told Ahab to gather all Israel and the prophets of Baal “to Mount Carmel”, and Ahab did.

daily.question: As the apostles watched Jesus being taken up, what received him out of their sight?
daily.explain: Acts 1:9: “as they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.”

daily.question: Elijah went up into heaven by a whirlwind.
daily.explain: 2 Kings 2:11: a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them, “and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.”

daily.question: Who was chosen by lot to be counted with the eleven apostles?
daily.explain: Acts 1:26: “They drew lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias; and he was counted with the eleven apostles.”

daily.question: How many times did Naaman dip himself in the Jordan?
daily.explain: 2 Kings 5:14: he “dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God”, and his flesh was restored like a little child’s.

daily.question: On the day of Pentecost, what appeared and rested on each of the believers?
daily.explain: Acts 2:3-4: “Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.” They were all filled with the Holy Spirit.

daily.question: What did Elisha make float on the water?
daily.explain: 2 Kings 6:5-6: a borrowed ax head fell into the water. The man of God threw a stick in there, “and made the iron float.”

daily.question: About 3,000 people were added to the believers on the day of Pentecost.
daily.explain: Acts 2:41: those who gladly received the message were baptized, and “There were added that day about three thousand souls.”

daily.question: How many years did the LORD add to King Hezekiah’s life?
daily.explain: 2 Kings 20:5-6: “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears.” Then God said, “I will add to your days fifteen years.”

daily.question: What was the temple gate called where the lame man was laid each day?
daily.explain: Acts 3:2: a man lame from birth was laid daily “at the door of the temple which is called Beautiful”, to ask for gifts.

daily.question: How long did it take to finish rebuilding the wall in Nehemiah’s day?
daily.explain: Nehemiah 6:15: “So the wall was finished in the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.”

daily.question: When Stephen was stoned, at whose feet did the witnesses lay their garments?
daily.explain: Acts 7:58: “The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.”

daily.question: Esther 2:7 gives Esther another name. What is it?
daily.explain: Esther 2:7: Mordecai “brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter”, and took her as his own daughter.

daily.question: Which prophet was the Ethiopian official reading in his chariot?
daily.explain: Acts 8:28: the official from Ethiopia “was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.”

daily.question: Haman ended up executed the very way he had planned for Mordecai.
daily.explain: Esther 7:10: “So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai.”

daily.question: How did the disciples help Saul escape by night?
choices: Hid him in a cart of hay
Sailed him away on a ship
Lowered him through the wall in a basket
daily.answer: Lowered him through the wall in a basket
daily.explain: Acts 9:25: “his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.”

daily.question: In which land did Job live?
daily.explain: Job 1:1: “There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job.” He was blameless and upright.

daily.question: Tabitha, the disciple at Joppa, was also known by which name?
daily.explain: Acts 9:36: “there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated means Dorcas.” She was full of good works.

daily.question: In the end, the LORD blessed Job more than at his beginning.
daily.explain: Job 42:12: “So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning.”

daily.question: In which city were the disciples first called Christians?
daily.explain: Acts 11:26: for a whole year they taught many people there, and “The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.”

daily.question: Which small creature does Proverbs tell the sluggard to watch and learn from?
daily.explain: Proverbs 6:6: “Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise”.

daily.question: When Peter knocked at the gate after his escape from prison, Rhoda let him in at once.
daily.explain: Acts 12:14: “When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy”, but ran in to tell the others he was there.

daily.question: In Isaiah’s vision, what did the seraph touch to his mouth?
choices: A live coal from the altar
daily.answer: A live coal from the altar
daily.explain: Isaiah 6:6-7: one of the seraphim flew to Isaiah with “a live coal in his hand”, touched his mouth, and said his sin was forgiven.

daily.question: What were Paul and Silas doing in prison about midnight?
daily.explain: Acts 16:25-26: “about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God”. Then a great earthquake opened all the doors.

daily.question: Where did God send Jeremiah to hear his words?
daily.explain: Jeremiah 18:2-4: he went “down to the potter’s house”, and watched the potter remake a spoiled clay vessel into another one.

daily.question: Who fell from a third floor window after falling asleep during Paul’s long talk?
daily.explain: Acts 20:9-10: “A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window”, fell asleep and fell. Paul embraced him and said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”

daily.question: In Ezekiel’s vision, what filled the valley?
daily.explain: Ezekiel 37:1-4: the valley “was full of bones”, and they were very dry. God asked, “Son of man, can these bones live?”

daily.question: Paul was born a Roman citizen.
daily.explain: Acts 22:27-28: the commander said he had bought his own citizenship. Paul answered, “But I was born a Roman.”

daily.question: What new name was Daniel given in Babylon?
daily.explain: Daniel 1:7: “to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar”. His friends were named Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

daily.question: On the island of Malta, what fastened onto Paul’s hand?
daily.explain: Acts 28:3: as Paul laid sticks on the fire, “a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.”

daily.question: In the king’s dream, what was the great statue’s head made of?
daily.explain: Daniel 2:32: “its head was of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze”.

daily.question: Paul’s letter to Philemon makes an appeal for which man?
daily.explain: Philemon 1:10: “I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whom I have become the father of in my chains”.

daily.question: How many men did King Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fire?
daily.explain: Daniel 3:24-25: three men had been thrown in bound, but the king said, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed.”

daily.question: What was the name of Timothy’s grandmother, whose sincere faith Paul remembered?
daily.explain: 2 Timothy 1:5: that sincere faith “lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice”, and Paul was sure it lived in Timothy too.

daily.question: At King Belshazzar’s feast, what wrote on the palace wall?
choices: The fingers of a man’s hand
daily.answer: The fingers of a man’s hand
daily.explain: Daniel 5:5: “the fingers of a man’s hand came out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace.”

daily.question: In Colossians, Paul calls Luke the beloved physician.
daily.explain: Colossians 4:14: “Luke the beloved physician and Demas greet you.”

daily.question: After the king signed the new law, Daniel stopped praying three times a day.
daily.explain: Daniel 6:10: with his windows open toward Jerusalem, Daniel “kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before.”

daily.question: On which island was John when he saw the visions of Revelation?
daily.explain: Revelation 1:9: John “was on the isle that is called Patmos because of God’s Word and the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

daily.question: How long was Jonah in the belly of the fish?
daily.explain: Jonah 1:17: “The LORD prepared a huge fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.”

daily.question: To how many assemblies was John told to send what he saw?
daily.explain: Revelation 1:11: “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies”, from Ephesus to Laodicea.

daily.question: Which small town does Micah 5:2 say a ruler in Israel will come from?
daily.explain: Micah 5:2: “But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will come out to me who is to be ruler in Israel”.

daily.question: Which assembly was told it was lukewarm, neither cold nor hot?
daily.explain: Revelation 3:14-15: the message “To the angel of the assembly in Laodicea” says, “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot.”

daily.question: When Jonah warned Nineveh, the people ignored him.
daily.explain: Jonah 3:5: “The people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least.”

daily.question: In John’s vision of the holy city, what was each gate made of?
daily.explain: Revelation 21:21: “The twelve gates were twelve pearls. Each one of the gates was made of one pearl.”

daily.question: In Zechariah 9:9, what is the coming King riding on?
daily.explain: Zechariah 9:9: “Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey”.

daily.question: How many kinds of fruit does the tree of life bear in Revelation 22?
daily.explain: Revelation 22:2: “the tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruits, yielding its fruit every month.”

jesusSaid.quote: I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.
jesusSaid.context: To the people in the temple, as he taught in the treasury. Whoever follows him has the light of life.

jesusSaid.quote: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
jesusSaid.context: To the crowds, right after he thanked the Father in prayer. An open invitation to anyone worn out.

jesusSaid.quote: Peace! Be still!
jesusSaid.context: Said to the sea as he rebuked the wind, after his frightened disciples woke him as the waves filled the boat.

jesusSaid.quote: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.
jesusSaid.context: At the house of Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, while the crowd grumbled that he had gone to stay with a sinner.

jesusSaid.quote: I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
jesusSaid.context: To the crowd that followed him to Capernaum after he fed them with the loaves. He is the bread that truly satisfies.

jesusSaid.quote: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
jesusSaid.context: The opening words of his teaching on the mountain, given to his disciples as the crowds gathered.

jesusSaid.quote: Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.
jesusSaid.context: Prayed from the cross at the place called The Skull, for the people who crucified him.

jesusSaid.quote: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples at supper, just after Judas had gone out into the night.

jesusSaid.quote: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.
jesusSaid.context: His answer when a lawyer among the Pharisees asked which is the greatest commandment in the law.

jesusSaid.quote: The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.
jesusSaid.context: To a scribe who asked which commandment is the greatest of all. Love for God comes first, then love for your neighbor.

jesusSaid.quote: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
jesusSaid.context: To listeners including Pharisees, soon after he healed a man born blind. His sheep know his voice and follow him.

jesusSaid.quote: There will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
jesusSaid.context: From his story of the lost sheep, told when Pharisees and scribes grumbled that he welcomed sinners.

jesusSaid.quote: Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.
jesusSaid.context: To the eleven disciples on a mountain in Galilee after he rose, as he sent them to make disciples of all nations.

jesusSaid.quote: Don’t be afraid, only believe.
jesusSaid.context: To Jairus, a synagogue ruler, the moment messengers came to say his daughter had died.

jesusSaid.quote: I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.
jesusSaid.context: To Thomas at supper, after he said the disciples didn’t know where Jesus was going or the way there.

jesusSaid.quote: Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.
jesusSaid.context: To one of the criminals crucified beside him, who asked Jesus to remember him when he came into his Kingdom.

jesusSaid.quote: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself.
jesusSaid.context: From his teaching on the mountain, after pointing to the birds and the lilies that God feeds and clothes.

jesusSaid.quote: Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?
jesusSaid.context: To Martha, who came out to meet him near Bethany after her brother Lazarus had been in the tomb four days.

jesusSaid.quote: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.
jesusSaid.context: To the lukewarm church in Laodicea, from the one called the Amen, the faithful and true witness.

jesusSaid.quote: For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
jesusSaid.context: To the twelve, after James and John asked to sit at his right and left hand in his glory.

jesusSaid.quote: I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples on his last night with them. He is the vine, they are the branches, and the Father tends them.

jesusSaid.quote: Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?
jesusSaid.context: Age 12, to his worried parents, when they found him after three days among the teachers in the temple.

jesusSaid.quote: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
jesusSaid.context: From his teaching on the mountain. The Father in heaven loves to give good things to those who ask him.

jesusSaid.quote: Whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.
jesusSaid.context: To a Samaritan woman who came to draw water while he rested at Jacob’s well.

jesusSaid.quote: Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.
jesusSaid.context: To the apostles when they came back and told him all they had done. So many came and went that they had no time to eat.

jesusSaid.quote: The very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples, whom he called friends, as a crowd of many thousands gathered. Not one sparrow is forgotten by God.

jesusSaid.quote: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples at supper, as he promised that the Father would send the Holy Spirit in his name.

jesusSaid.quote: Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you.
jesusSaid.context: From his teaching on the mountain, going beyond the old saying about loving your neighbor and hating your enemy.

jesusSaid.quote: I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
jesusSaid.context: To Saul near Damascus, after a light from the sky shone around him and he fell to the ground.

jesusSaid.quote: It is finished!
jesusSaid.context: On the cross, after he received the vinegar, just before he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

jesusSaid.quote: Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples and a great crowd on a level place, where people came to hear him and to be healed.

jesusSaid.quote: Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.
jesusSaid.context: To the brothers Simon Peter and Andrew, who were casting a net into the Sea of Galilee.

jesusSaid.quote: If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.
jesusSaid.context: To a father who begged him to help his suffering son, if he could do anything at all.

jesusSaid.quote: Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.
jesusSaid.context: To Thomas, who had missed Jesus’ first visit to the disciples, eight days later, once he saw his hands and side.

jesusSaid.quote: Don’t be afraid. I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever.
jesusSaid.context: To John on the island of Patmos, who fell at his feet like a dead man when he saw him.

jesusSaid.quote: Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.
jesusSaid.context: When little children were brought for him to lay hands on and pray for, and his disciples rebuked them.

jesusSaid.quote: Unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.
jesusSaid.context: To Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler of the Jews, who came to him by night.

jesusSaid.quote: Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.
jesusSaid.context: His prayer on the Mount of Olives, kneeling about a stone’s throw from his disciples.

jesusSaid.quote: Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.
jesusSaid.context: To Pharisees and Herodians who tried to trap him with a question about paying taxes to Caesar.

jesusSaid.quote: Come and eat breakfast!
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples on the shore of the Sea of Tiberias after he rose, beside a fire with fish and bread.

jesusSaid.quote: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.
jesusSaid.context: Teaching his disciples about agreeing together in prayer. He is with even two or three who gather in his name.

jesusSaid.quote: Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.
jesusSaid.context: To a woman who wept at his feet and anointed them in a Pharisee’s house, while the other guests wondered who could forgive sins.

jesusSaid.quote: If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!
jesusSaid.context: He stood and cried out on the last and greatest day of the Feast of Booths.

jesusSaid.quote: Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life.
jesusSaid.context: To the church in Smyrna, facing poverty and prison, from the one who was dead and has come to life.

jesusSaid.quote: Because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.
jesusSaid.context: From his picture of the King judging the nations. Kindness to the hungry, the stranger and the sick is kindness to him.

jesusSaid.quote: Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM.
jesusSaid.context: In the temple, to people who said he wasn’t yet fifty years old and couldn’t have seen Abraham.

jesusSaid.quote: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me.
jesusSaid.context: To the eleven and their friends in Jerusalem, who were terrified and thought they were seeing a spirit.

jesusSaid.quote: The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.
jesusSaid.context: His message as he came into Galilee preaching the Good News, after John was taken into custody.

jesusSaid.quote: Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
jesusSaid.context: His reply after Philip and Andrew told him that some Greeks at the feast wanted to see him.

jesusSaid.quote: Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
jesusSaid.context: To Pharisees who asked why he ate with tax collectors and sinners, at a meal after he called Matthew.

jesusSaid.quote: If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
jesusSaid.context: Said to all, just after Peter answered that Jesus is the Christ of God.

jesusSaid.quote: Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples at supper, just after he told Peter he would deny him three times.

jesusSaid.quote: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.
jesusSaid.context: To the apostles, just before he was taken up and a cloud hid him from their sight.

jesusSaid.quote: Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
jesusSaid.context: From his teaching on the mountain, where he told his listeners they are the light of the world.

jesusSaid.quote: Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.
jesusSaid.context: To the crowd, after a man asked him to tell his brother to divide an inheritance with him.

jesusSaid.quote: I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut.
jesusSaid.context: To the church in Philadelphia, which had little power but kept his word and didn’t deny his name.

jesusSaid.quote: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
jesusSaid.context: To Peter in Gethsemane, when he came back from praying and found the disciples asleep.

jesusSaid.quote: Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.
jesusSaid.context: To his disciples behind locked doors on the evening of the day he rose, after he showed them his hands and side.

jesusSaid.quote: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.
jesusSaid.context: At the close of John’s vision. In the same passage he names himself: Jesus, who sent his angel to the churches.

jesusSaid.quote: Yes, I am coming soon.
jesusSaid.context: From the one who testifies to all John saw, near the very end of the Bible. John replies, “Yes, come, Lord Jesus!”

places.title: God creates the world
places.place: Everywhere: the heavens and the earth, all that exists
places.when: In the beginning, before anything else was made
places.text: The Bible’s first sentence names no city and no date. It starts with God and all he made: “In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.”

places.title: The garden of Eden
places.place: A garden planted in Eden, in the east; its exact site is not known
places.when: At the very start of human history, as Genesis tells it
places.text: Genesis says a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, then split into four rivers. One of them is the Euphrates, which still flows through the Middle East today.

places.title: Noah’s ark comes to rest
places.place: The mountains of Ararat, a highland region in what is now eastern Turkey and Armenia
places.when: While the flood waters went down, on the 17th day of the 7th month, Genesis says
places.text: Genesis says the ark settled “on Ararat’s mountains,” naming a range rather than one peak, so the exact spot is not known.

places.title: Abram’s family leaves Ur
places.place: Ur of the Chaldees, an ancient city of Mesopotamia, usually placed in southern Iraq
places.when: In the days of Abram’s father Terah, long before Israel was a nation
places.text: Terah set out from Ur with his son Abram, Abram’s wife Sarai and his grandson Lot, heading for the land of Canaan. But they stopped in Haran and settled there.

places.title: Abram sets out from Haran
places.place: Haran, a town in northern Mesopotamia, in what is now southeastern Turkey
places.when: When Abram was 75 years old
places.text: Abram left Haran just as the LORD had told him. He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all their possessions and their people, and set out for the land of Canaan.

places.title: God’s promise at Shechem
places.place: Shechem, by the oak of Moreh, in the hill country of Canaan
places.when: When Abram first reached Canaan, while Canaanites still lived in the land
places.text: Here the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” Abram built an altar to the LORD on the spot.

places.title: Jacob’s family moves to Egypt
places.place: The land of Goshen, usually placed in the eastern Nile Delta of Egypt
places.when: In the days when Joseph governed Egypt for Pharaoh
places.text: Joseph got his chariot ready and rode out to meet his father Jacob in Goshen. When they met, Joseph fell on his neck and wept for a long while.

places.title: The burning bush
places.place: Horeb, the mountain of God, at the far side of the wilderness
places.when: While Moses kept the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian
places.text: Moses led the sheep to Horeb, the mountain of God. There the LORD’s angel appeared to him in a flame of fire from the middle of a bush, and the bush was not burned up.

places.title: Israel leaves Egypt
places.place: From Rameses to Succoth, the first stretch of the road out of Egypt
places.when: At the end of 430 years in Egypt, on the night of the first Passover
places.text: About 600,000 men set out on foot, plus children, flocks and herds. They left in such a hurry that their bread dough had no time to rise, so they baked it unleavened.

places.title: Crossing the Red Sea
places.place: The Red Sea, at the edge of Egypt; the exact crossing point is not known
places.when: Soon after Israel left Egypt, with Pharaoh’s army close behind
places.text: Moses stretched out his hand. A strong east wind blew all night and turned the sea into dry land, and Israel walked through with walls of water on their right and on their left.

places.title: God meets Moses at Sinai
places.place: Mount Sinai, in the wilderness of Sinai; its exact location is debated
places.when: In the third month after Israel left Egypt
places.text: Israel set up camp in the wilderness right in front of the mountain. Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain with a message for the people.

places.title: The walls of Jericho fall
places.place: Jericho, an ancient city in the Jordan Valley, close to the Jordan River
places.when: Soon after Israel crossed the Jordan into Canaan, led by Joshua
places.text: The priests blew the trumpets and the people gave a great shout. The wall fell down flat, and everyone went straight up into the city.

places.title: David faces Goliath
places.place: The valley of Elah in Judah, between two armies on facing hills
places.when: In the days of King Saul, while David was still a young shepherd
places.text: The Philistines camped between Socoh and Azekah, and Saul’s army lined up in the valley of Elah. Each army stood on a mountain, with the valley between them.

places.title: David takes Jerusalem
places.place: Jerusalem, then a Jebusite hilltop stronghold called Zion
places.when: After the elders of all Israel anointed David king at Hebron
places.text: The Jebusites boasted that even the blind and the lame could keep David out. But David took the stronghold of Zion, and it became known as David’s city.

places.title: Solomon builds the temple
places.place: Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite
places.when: In King Solomon’s 4th year, in the second month, nearly a thousand years before Jesus
places.text: Solomon built the LORD’s house on the spot his father David had chosen, the place where the LORD had appeared to David.

places.title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
places.place: Mount Carmel, a ridge in northern Israel that runs to the Mediterranean coast
places.when: In the days of King Ahab and Queen Jezebel
places.text: Elijah had Ahab gather all Israel here, along with 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of Asherah who ate at Jezebel’s table.

places.title: Jerusalem falls to Babylon
places.place: Jerusalem, burned by Babylon’s army, its people taken away to Babylon
places.when: In the 19th year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, nearly 600 years before Jesus
places.text: Babylon’s captain of the guard burned the LORD’s house, the king’s house and every great house. The army broke down Jerusalem’s walls, and the people left in the city were carried away captive.

places.title: The exiles go home
places.place: From Babylon, across the Persian Empire, back to Jerusalem in Judah
places.when: In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, after Babylon fell to him
places.text: God stirred the heart of Cyrus, and he sent word through his whole kingdom: any of the LORD’s people could go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the LORD.

places.title: Nehemiah rebuilds the wall
places.place: Jerusalem, its walls broken down and its gates burned
places.when: In the 20th year of Artaxerxes, king of Persia
places.text: Nehemiah told the people: you see the trouble we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste and its gates are burned. “Come, let’s build up the wall of Jerusalem.”

places.title: An angel visits Mary
places.place: Nazareth, a town in Galilee, in the north of the land
places.when: In the days of King Herod, six months after Elizabeth conceived John
places.text: God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, to a virgin named Mary. She was pledged to be married to Joseph, a man from the family of King David.

places.title: Jesus is born
places.place: Bethlehem, a small town in Judea, south of Jerusalem
places.when: In the days of King Herod, when Caesar Augustus ordered a census
places.text: Joseph went up from Nazareth to Bethlehem, David’s city, to be enrolled with Mary. There she gave birth to her firstborn son and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room in the inn.

places.title: Jesus is baptized
places.place: The Jordan River, where John was baptizing
places.when: When Jesus was about 30, at the start of his public work
places.text: Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan. The river runs south from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea.

places.title: Jesus calls fishermen
places.place: The shore of the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake in the north
places.when: Early in Jesus’ public work, soon after his baptism
places.text: Jesus saw Simon and Andrew casting a net into the lake and said, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.” They left their nets at once and followed him.

places.title: Jesus makes Capernaum home
places.place: Capernaum, a fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
places.when: After John the Baptizer was arrested
places.text: Jesus left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, a town by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali. It became his home base in Galilee.

places.title: The woman at the well
places.place: Jacob’s well at Sychar, in Samaria, between Judea and Galilee
places.when: About the sixth hour of the day, as Jesus traveled from Judea to Galilee
places.text: Tired from the journey, Jesus sat down by Jacob’s well, near land Jacob had given his son Joseph. A Samaritan woman came to draw water, and Jesus said, “Give me a drink.”

places.title: Jesus raises Lazarus
places.place: Bethany, a village on the Mount of Olives, close to Jerusalem
places.when: Shortly before Jesus’ last Passover in Jerusalem
places.text: By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days. Bethany sat close to Jerusalem, only about 15 stadia from the city.

places.title: The Last Supper
places.place: A large, furnished upper room in a house in Jerusalem
places.when: On the day of unleavened bread, when the Passover lamb was sacrificed
places.text: Jesus sent Peter and John into the city to follow a man carrying a pitcher of water. The owner of that house would show them a large upper room, and there they prepared the Passover.

places.title: Jesus prays in Gethsemane
places.place: Gethsemane, a garden on the Mount of Olives, across the Kidron brook
places.when: Late on the night of the Last Supper, before his arrest
places.text: After the meal, Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane and said, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”

places.title: Jesus is crucified
places.place: Golgotha, the Place of a Skull, near the city of Jerusalem
places.when: On the Preparation Day of the Passover, when Pontius Pilate was governor
places.text: Carrying his own cross, Jesus went out to Golgotha. Pilate’s sign on the cross read JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS, and since the place was near the city, many people read it.

places.title: The empty tomb
places.place: A new tomb in a garden, near the place where Jesus was crucified
places.when: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark
places.text: Mary Magdalene came to the tomb before daybreak and saw that the stone had been taken away from it.

places.title: The road to Emmaus
places.place: Emmaus, a village 60 stadia from Jerusalem; its exact site is uncertain
places.when: That very same day, the day the stone was found rolled away
places.text: Two followers walked along, talking about everything that had happened. Jesus himself came near and walked with them, but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.

places.title: The Spirit comes at Pentecost
places.place: Jerusalem, where devout Jews from every nation were staying
places.when: On the day of Pentecost, the harvest feast about 50 days after Passover
places.text: Jesus’ followers were together in one place. A sound like a rushing wind filled the house, tongues like fire rested on each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit.

places.title: Saul on the Damascus road
places.place: The road to Damascus, an ancient city in Syria, northeast of Galilee
places.when: Soon after Stephen’s death, while Saul was hunting the believers
places.text: Saul set out with letters from the high priest to arrest followers of the Way in Damascus. As he came near the city, a light from the sky suddenly shone around him.

places.title: Sent out from Antioch
places.place: Antioch, a great city of Roman Syria, today Antakya in Turkey
places.when: In the early days of the church, while Barnabas and Saul taught at Antioch
places.text: As the church in Antioch served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul. The church prayed, laid hands on them and sent them out.

places.title: Paul comes to Philippi
places.place: Philippi, a Roman colony and leading city of Macedonia, in northern Greece
places.when: On Paul’s travels, right after his vision of a man from Macedonia
places.text: On the Sabbath, Paul and his companions went outside the city to a riverside, looking for a place of prayer. They sat down and spoke with the women gathered there.

places.title: Paul speaks in Athens
places.place: Athens in Greece, at the Areopagus, the hill where the city’s council met
places.when: On Paul’s travels, while he waited in Athens for Silas and Timothy
places.text: The people of Athens loved to hear anything new. Standing in the Areopagus, Paul told them he had found an altar inscribed TO AN UNKNOWN GOD, and he had come to tell them about that God.

places.title: Paul stays in Corinth
places.place: Corinth, a busy trading city on the narrow isthmus of southern Greece
places.when: On Paul’s travels, when Gallio was the Roman governor of Achaia
places.text: In a night vision the Lord told Paul not to be afraid but to keep speaking, because he had many people in that city. So Paul stayed a year and six months, teaching God’s word.

places.title: Two years in Ephesus
places.place: Ephesus, a great port city of the province of Asia, on the coast of today’s Turkey
places.when: On Paul’s later travels, while Apollos was in Corinth
places.text: Paul taught in Ephesus for two years, until everyone who lived in the province of Asia, both Jews and Greeks, had heard the word of the Lord.

places.title: Paul in Rome
places.place: Rome, the capital city of the Roman Empire
places.when: After a long sea voyage and a shipwreck, while Paul waited to stand before Caesar
places.text: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house, welcoming everyone who came. He preached God’s Kingdom and taught about Jesus boldly, and no one stopped him.

places.title: John’s vision on Patmos
places.place: Patmos, a small island in the Aegean Sea, off the coast of today’s Turkey
places.when: On the Lord’s Day, while John shared in his fellow believers’ hardships
places.text: John says he was on the island called Patmos because of God’s Word and the testimony of Jesus. There he saw the visions he was told to write in a book.

parts.text: After a night of catching nothing, Simon let down his nets at Jesus’ word. The catch filled two boats till they began to sink. Simon fell at Jesus’ knees: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.” Jesus said, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive.”
parts.next: Next: Peter steps out of the boat onto the waves.

parts.text: Seeing Jesus on the water, Peter said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.” Jesus said, “Come!” Peter walked on the water, but when he saw the strong wind he began to sink. He cried, “Lord, save me!” and Jesus caught him.
parts.next: Next: the night Peter said he never knew him.

parts.text: After Jesus’ arrest, Peter sat by a fire in a courtyard. Three times people said he had been with Jesus, and three times Peter denied it. A rooster crowed. The Lord turned and looked at Peter, and Peter went out and wept bitterly.
parts.next: Next: breakfast by the lake, and three questions from the risen Jesus.

parts.text: After breakfast, the risen Jesus asked Peter three times whether he loved him. Grieved by the third question, Peter said, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Each time Jesus gave him a task: feed my lambs, tend my sheep.
parts.next: Next: the man who denied Jesus speaks up for him before a huge crowd.

parts.text: Weeks later, Peter told a crowd that God had made Jesus “both Lord and Christ”. Cut to the heart, they asked, “Brothers, what shall we do?” That day about 3,000 people were added. The man who once said he never knew Jesus now spoke for him.
Saul approved of Stephen’s death. A great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and believers scattered. Saul went from house to house, dragging men and women off to prison.
parts.next: Next: a blinding light on the road to Damascus.

parts.text: Near Damascus, a light from the sky flashed around Saul. He fell to the ground and heard a voice: “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” It was Jesus. Saul got up blind, was led by the hand into the city, and for three days he did not eat or drink.
parts.next: Next: God sends a believer to the very man everyone feared.

parts.text: The Lord sent a believer named Ananias. He laid his hands on Saul and called him “Brother Saul”. Something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and he could see. He was baptized, and right away he proclaimed in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.
parts.next: Next: an earthquake at midnight throws open a prison.

parts.text: Years later, Paul and Silas sat in prison, praying and singing at midnight. An earthquake threw the doors open and loosened every chain. The jailer was about to kill himself, but Paul shouted, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”
parts.next: Next: after storms and a shipwreck, Paul finally reaches Rome.

parts.text: At last Paul came to Rome, a prisoner with a soldier to guard him. Believers walked out as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet him. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage. The man who once dragged believers to prison was now welcomed by them.

A Hebrew mother hid her baby boy for three months. When she could hide him no longer, she put him in a papyrus basket coated with tar and set it in the reeds by the river. His sister watched. Then Pharaoh’s daughter came to bathe, opened the basket, and the baby cried.
parts.next: Next: years later, a bush on fire that does not burn up.

parts.text: God called to Moses from the middle of a bush: “Moses! Moses!” He told him to take off his sandals, for this was holy ground. Then God said he had seen his people’s suffering in Egypt, and he was sending Moses to Pharaoh to bring them out.
parts.next: Next: Pharaoh’s army closes in, with the sea in front of them.

parts.text: Moses stretched out his hand, and a strong east wind blew all night. Israel walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on both sides. Pharaoh’s chariots followed them in, but at dawn the waters returned and covered the whole army.
parts.next: Next: a mountain wrapped in cloud and fire, and God calls Moses up.

parts.text: God called Moses up Mount Sinai to receive stone tablets with the law. A cloud covered the mountain, and to the people below, the LORD’s glory looked like a devouring fire. Moses walked into the cloud and stayed on the mountain 40 days and 40 nights.
parts.next: Next: Moses climbs one last mountain and sees the promised land.

parts.text: At the end of his life, Moses climbed Mount Nebo. From the top, God showed him the whole land promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and told him he would see it but not go in. Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in Moab.

Samuel asked Jesse, “Are all your children here?” Only the youngest was missing, out keeping the sheep. When David came in, the LORD said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.” From that day the LORD’s Spirit came mightily on David.
parts.next: Next: a shepherd boy, a sling and a giant.

parts.text: Goliath came with sword, spear and javelin. David told him, “I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies.” He ran toward the giant, slung one stone and struck him in the forehead. Goliath fell on his face, and there was no sword in David’s hand.
parts.next: Next: King Saul hunts David, and David gets a perfect chance for revenge.

parts.text: Saul stepped into the very cave where David and his men were hiding. David’s men urged him to strike. Instead David secretly cut off the edge of Saul’s robe, and even that troubled his heart. He would not harm the LORD’s anointed, and he held his men back.
parts.next: Next: the shepherd finally becomes king.

parts.text: The elders of all Israel came to David at Hebron and anointed him king over Israel. He was 30 years old when he began to reign, and he reigned 40 years: seven and a half in Hebron, then 33 in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah.
parts.next: Next: King David’s worst sin, and the prophet who confronted him.

parts.text: David had taken Uriah’s wife and had Uriah killed. The prophet Nathan told him to his face, “You are the man!” David said, “I have sinned against the LORD.” Nathan answered, “The LORD also has put away your sin.”

Jacob loved Joseph most and made him a tunic of many colors, so his brothers hated him. Then Joseph told them a dream: their sheaves of grain bowed down to his. “Will you indeed reign over us?” they asked, and hated him even more.
parts.next: Next: his brothers throw him into a pit.

parts.text: When Joseph reached his brothers, they stripped off his tunic and threw him into an empty pit. Then a caravan came by on its way to Egypt. Judah said they should sell him rather than kill him. Joseph was sold for 20 pieces of silver and taken to Egypt.
parts.next: Next: a slave in Egypt rises to rule the land.

parts.text: Because God had shown Joseph the meaning of Pharaoh’s dreams, Pharaoh said no one was so wise. He put his own signet ring on Joseph’s hand and a gold chain on his neck, and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
parts.next: Next: his brothers arrive in Egypt and bow down to him.

parts.text: Joseph’s brothers came to Egypt to buy food and bowed before the governor with their faces to the ground. They had no idea it was Joseph. He knew them at once, and he remembered his dreams.
parts.next: Next: Joseph can’t hold back any longer.

parts.text: Joseph sent everyone else out and wept so loudly that Pharaoh’s house heard. “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt,” he told his terrified brothers. Then he told them not to be angry with themselves, “for God sent me before you to preserve life.”

Esther, raised by her cousin Mordecai as his own daughter, was taken to King Ahasuerus. She won the favor of everyone who saw her. The king loved her more than all the others, set the royal crown on her head and made her queen.
parts.next: Next: a proud official plots to wipe out Esther’s people.

parts.text: Mordecai would not bow down to Haman. Haman was furious, and since he knew Mordecai was a Jew, he decided to destroy not just Mordecai but all the Jews in the whole kingdom.
parts.next: Next: Mordecai asks Esther to risk her life.

parts.text: Mordecai urged Esther to go to the king: “Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” Going in was against the law. Esther asked the Jews to fast for her three days, then said, “If I perish, I perish.”
parts.next: Next: Haman plans a royal parade for himself, and gets a shock.

parts.text: The king asked Haman what should be done for the man he delighted to honor. Sure it meant himself, Haman described a royal robe, the king’s horse and a public parade. Then the king said: do it for Mordecai. Haman had to lead his enemy through the city square.
parts.next: Next: at a banquet, Esther finally names the enemy.

parts.text: At the banquet, Esther named the man behind the plot: “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!” The king rose in his wrath. Haman was hanged on the very gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Her courage had turned the plot back on its maker.
